projects.title: [开源推荐] agent-graph：用 git graph 管理多个编程 agent 的交互设计与原型
projects.author: jihe520

github.name: jihe520/agent-graph
github.description: 把 ADE（agent 开发环境）的主交互元素从「会话」换成「git graph」的一次交互探索

projects.summary: 同时跑好几个编程 agent 时，会话列表很难回答这些问题：谁在哪个分支和 worktree 上改代码、谁派出了子 agent、谁在等你批准、谁做完了可以合并。这个项目把 agent 开发环境（ADE）的主视图换成 git graph：agent 直接挂在分支上显示状态，批准、合并在图上就地完成，会话退到侧栏。仓库包含设计规范、一份可以直接发给 agent 的实现提示词，以及一个浏览器打开即用的单文件原型。 亮点 换了主元素：同类工具大多是「会话列表 + 对话」，这里以 git graph 为主视图，agent 的状态、分支、worktree、子 agent 和提交历史都在一张图上 不绑定宿主：交付的是设计规范和提示词，而不是又一个 ADE。在能改源码的 ADE（比如 t3code 的 fork）里把提示词发给 agent，它会先调研、给出概念映射和计划，确认后分阶段实现 多个 harness 同屏：Claude Code、Codex、Pi 等用颜色和头像区分 原型零依赖：单个 HTML 文件，可

projects.title: Show HN: Mallard: Git for the age of AI agents
projects.author: rika321
projects.summary: We started Mallard to make it easier to share our agent sessions and build things together. We spend much of our working day talking to Claude and Codex. Those conversations include the ideas, designs, and decisions behind our work. However they often stay on one machine, without backups or an easy way to share them. 3 months. 10 accounts on 20× plans. 100 billion tokens later, Mallard finally hatched. Share and back up agent sessions using Cloudflare R2, Dropbox, or Mallard Cloud. Explore the discussions and design decisions behind PRs, including Mallard’s hatching logs. Pull and resume sessions in Codex or Claude Code with the original context. For teams, Anthropic internally uses cloud VMs and Claude Tag so that teammates can work in shared agent conversations and pick up where others left off. Mallard lets teams achieve the same goal at almost zero cost, without any cloud VMs. We want Mallard to be free and easy to use for everyone, rich or poor. We built a lightweight version of GIT and reworked our storage protocol, removing CAS so Mallard can work with any cloud storage that supports LIST and PUT APIs. Bring your own storage or use Mallard Cloud. No Git server or expensive sandbox required. We also added one-click sign-in for Dropbox and Cloudflare R2, so anyone can connect their own cloud storage to Mallard in just a few clicks. We don’t think the internet, recommendation algorithms, or AI should be in the hands of just a few people. We hope Mallard helps more people share their work, find an audience, and have their voices heard. Free and MIT licensed. Available on macOS and Windows. Website: https://mallard-ai.com/ GitHub: https://github.com/Git4Agent/mallard-app

projects.title: Show HN: Garrul – Comments system for your site on a single Cloudflare Worker
projects.author: KingPinX
projects.summary: I needed a comments system for my blog (running on Cloudflare & Astro), the other options I tried didn't work out as I wanted. So Garrul was born, it uses one Cloudflare Worker with D1 + KV, in your own account. No container, no VPS, no DB server to manage or worry about! Most sites fit the free tier, I am using it for 5 lowish traffic sites with zero issues. I wanted privacy of commenters to be primary here, along with ease of use so that was always the basis of many decisions I took along the way. For example, we never store IP addresses directly. Every IP is HMAC hashed, ipv6 is truncated first. I have worked steadily on optimizations every chance, e.g. instead of having few separate calls for the config, session, first set of comments, subscription state etc it's all a single call. Posting costs a single call, you can even have a reaction only mode for specific pages/articles. The anti-spam call and turnstile call only happen when user actually focuses the comment posting embed. The math works out to roughly 100k pageviews/day on the free tier. The widget embed itself is limited to 30KB gzipped, with the CI set to fail above that so we don't ship massive embeds. One of the larger issues with trying to stick within Cloudflare free tier is the 1000 writes/day for KV. We used to have per request KV Cache, that burned me when I woke up to my first bot swarm browsing thru the site and locking out the comments for the whole day. That made me move the cache to the cache API. Demo (anonymous posting works) : https://garrul.com/#comments I would appreciate any feedback on improving the system. Optimization and security are my current focus, so anything anyone can help with there will be immensely appreciated. Some of the feature highlights : Threaded markdown enabled comments OAuth (Google, Facebook, X, Discord, GitHub logins) or Anon posting pinned comments, opt in reply emails, digest of posts to moderators, and a telegram bot to moderate the whole thing from telegram itself (I use this telegram bot daily). Multiple languages, and ability to import from multiple systems like Disqus and Remark42 among others. Licensed as Apache2.0. So it is tied to Cloudflare for now, meaning even tho Cloudflare D1 is simply SQLite, you can't just run it anywhere other than CF. In our case your data can be exported as a plain SQLite dump (via npm run db:export) or json or CSV from the admin panel, whenever you need it. I used AI assistance heavily for this, coding, tests, and red-teaming. I review what goes in and CI catches a lot.

projects.title: Show HN: Duckity – Abuse protection for the AI agent era
projects.author: nyeki
projects.summary: Hey there! I'm Rafa, founder of Duckity. Have you ever been stopped by "prove you're a human" before logging in, signing up, or sending a friend request? Your users have too, and it sucks. Duckity allows you to define what good behavior looks like instead, and deters any activity going against that with invisible CPU work and temporary freezes that slow down malicious activity. You get - Completely invisible protection, - Silk-smooth UX, - Way more powerful customization of its behavior, - To ditch captchas! Bots = bad, humans = good doesn't hold up anymore. People use AI agents to do things on their behalf, and they shouldn't be treated as adversarial. Meanwhile, is spam any good as long as it's human-made? Also, Duckity is backed by a cryptography primitive called a VDF. Since crypto is cross-platform, so is Duckity! If you have a native app, it's a great moment to bring login flows in-app while staying protected. I'm using it on my package manager, which lets me sign up and log in users directly from the terminal. I'm still working on it a lot, and I made sure to write good docs to help you get started. Any feedback, tips, or info is really useful and more than welcome.

projects.title: Show HN: I built Knemora – An Open-source AI Second brain
projects.author: flaterra
projects.summary: Hi HN, my name is Federico. I’m an Italian graphic designer and full stack developer. In recent months, there has been a lot of talk about the "second brain" articles and YouTube videos; everyone is still discussing it, but I see a significant difference between that and what the concept of a second brain means to me. For me, the concept of a "second brain" is about building a 100% private knowledge base which means not uploading my own files (containing sensitive data) to be processed via cloud-based inference. I’ve seen many videos discussing how to "build your own second brain" using Claude Code and Obsidian. I’ve always wondered: why should I upload my personal files such as certificates, my children’s birth certificates, or other sensitive personal data—to a service like Claude, where I have no idea where those files end up or who might be reading them? Furthermore, why should I rely on a graph-based viewer like Obsidian, effectively making myself dependent on third parties, paid services, and software that I have to install directly onto my own device? From that came the idea to develop Knemora, an open-source, local-first project that runs locally by leveraging local inference. The challenge involved: - choosing a modular architecture - ensuring ease of use via a CLI and a web interface - avoiding the need for users to install third-party software on their own devices - enabling setup in just 2 CLI commands - ensuring suitability for both developers (tech-savvy users) and various private organisations (such as notary offices, dental practices, insurance companies, etc.). So far knemora includes the following features: - local inference via llama.cpp (with built-in support for cross-platform operation) - ability to use "knemora-tested" models or custom models from Hugging Face; simply run the command `./knemora load --model hf:<Hugging Face model name>` - a chatbot agent that answers questions and searches through your knowledge base based on your natural-language queries - a knowledge agent built using Google’s ADK 2.0 (my agentic orchestrator) - portable knowledge, markdown files are linked following the "LLM WIKI" pattern (as proposed by Andrej Karpathy) - BM25-based retrieval (no vector database required) - original documents are preserved and marked as (immutable) - dataset analysis powered by Polars Currently, it is available only for macOS with Apple Silicon chips, but it will soon be available for Windows and Linux as well. Version v0.2.0, available today on GitHub, covers these additional features and improvements: - conversation continuity - automatic language matching - gemma 4 joins the tested model registry - more curated models ahead - more control over chat - wiki / direct chat modes - fast / deep chat modes - stronger knowledge compilation My goal is to make Knemora more stable, responsive, easier to use and keep moving toward a stable v1.0.0. Thank you! Watch the alpha demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kl5qNrWPOnY Explore the project: https://knemora.space Code and documentation: https://github.com/federicolaterra/knemora

projects.title: Show HN: Vectoys – 3D devices for landing pages, drawn as plain SVG
projects.author: mertduzgun
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Mert. Vectoys is a free, MIT-licensed set of interactive "toys" for landing pages: a MacBook that opens and kickflips on scroll, a keyboard you can actually type on, an iPhone running a small to-do app, keycaps, an envelope, and more. I built many Mac and iOS apps over the last two months and found myself explaining products with the device frames is working and looking better than plain text. I got Opus 5.5 draw me realistic devices but on each website it created the 3d rendering engine from scratch so I extracted that into an open source library. Agents are good at drawing with SVG but not that good. I had to do 15+ iterations for the laptop devices to make them look good. I'm sharing all of them so you don't have to do the same. Everything is plain SVG and HTML. No WebGL, no canvas, no images. The devices are drawn with real perspective math, so you can grab any toy and turn it around, or open it full screen. The screens are live, selectable HTML that turns with the device. Some facts about the library: - Server rendering is checked: every toy renders twice on the server and the markup must match exactly. - Each toy stays under 96 KB. - Animations respect prefers-reduced-motion. You copy a toy into your project with `npx @vinena/vectoys-cli add laptop` (or `npx shadcn add https://vectoys.com/r/laptop.json `), or use the React package. There's also a one-line prompt you can give a coding agent, and it picks and places toys on your landing page for you. Even though I used this for device drawing, possibilities are endless. You can get your agent draw whatever you want. I use it on my own sites (snug.so is the first). If you think something like that would be cool or helpful to you, I'd love you to try the prompt share the result with me. Thanks for reading!

projects.summary: 我做了一个 tmux 插件，帮助经常同时使用多个 AI 编程助手的人，在电脑重启后恢复工作现场。 用 tmux 开多个窗口跑 AI 编程任务很方便，但重启后，即使通过 tmux-resurrect 找回了窗口布局，还得逐个找到并恢复原来的 AI 对话。特别是同一个项目目录里开了多个对话时，很容易记不清哪个窗格对应哪条会话。 tmux-agent-resurrect 是 tmux-resurrect 的配套插件。保存工作区时，它会识别每个窗格里的 AI 对话；恢复时，除了还原窗口布局，也会在对应窗格中重新打开原来的对话。目前内置支持 Codex 和 OpenCode，也可以通过 Python 适配器扩展其他命令行工具。 为什么值得推荐 这个工具适合在 tmux 里并行处理多个项目或任务的人：保存一次工作区，重启后就能把窗口和对话一起找回来，不必逐个翻找会话。即使多个窗格处于同一个项目目录，也会尽量识别各自对应的对话；无法明确判断时，插件会跳过该窗格，避免恢复错会话。 项目支持脚本安装和 TPM 安装。需要说明的是，它恢复的是已保存的对话，不会让关机时中断的命令或模型回复从中途继续执行。

Browse all accessible images, just screenshots, or a specific album. Start on-device analysis for your chosen scope. Images and recognized text are not uploaded to a developer-operated server. Text search requires analysis, and similar-image suggestions should be reviewed manually.

projects.title: 【工具自荐】BayesChat：iPhone / iPad 上自带 Key 接模型、可挂远程 MCP 的聊天客户端
projects.author: fan3cn
projects.summary: 我是开发者。BayesChat 是一个 iPhone / iPad 上的 AI 聊天客户端，做的事和 Jan、Cherry Studio 这类桌面端一样——自带 Key 接自己的模型——只是搬到了手机上： 任何 OpenAI / Anthropic 兼容端点都能接：OpenAI Chat Completions 与 Responses、Anthropic Messages、Gemini 的 OpenAI 兼容层、OpenRouter，也可以填本机跑的 Ollama / LM Studio 的地址。 能挂远程 MCP 服务器，按工具单独开关。iOS 起不了子进程，所以只支持远程 Streamable HTTP，stdio Server 用不了——这条写在应用里，不是隐藏条件。 没有账号、没有同步服务器、没有统计 SDK：Key 存系统 Keychain，对话存本地。 两个在手机上比较少见的地方，可能值得占「本周工具」里的一行：一是「一次配置换一个助手」的预设，把提示词、模型、参数、记忆和工具选择打包成一个可切换的单元；二是长回答的渲染，Markdown、KaTeX、代码高亮都在一个 WKWebView 里，只重绘正在输出的那一块，几千字的回答不会逐段重排。 免费下载，MCP 工具、预设、记忆等属一次性买断（14.99 美元）解锁。App Store 上评分人数还是个位数，它还很早期，所以如果你看完觉得不值得登，我完全理解。 一个限制先讲：没有在中国区上架，国内读者点 App Store 链接会跳到空页面，只能从官网走。如果这条对周刊读者来说太别扭，那它就不合适，直说即可。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】纸间：浏览器里的 AI 论文阅读器，为大模型时代更优雅的读论文而生
projects.author: Robbings

github.name: Robbings/Paperpane
github.description: 纸间（Paperpane）是一款浏览器论文阅读扩展，支持 PDF 对照翻译、选段提问、公式复制、批注笔记和文献库同步。

projects.summary: 纸间是一款浏览器扩展，用来在浏览器里阅读论文。在 arXiv、Google Scholar 等页面点一下即可打开论文，右侧自动生成概览，论文自动识别图表公式；阅读时可以对照翻译，划选文字或用提供的工具之间截图或者选择自动识别的图表公式，就可以直接让 AI 解释或提问，回答会标注出处，点击即可跳回原文。 为什么做这个 我原来用 Zotero 读论文，但它对 AI 的支持有限，有很多开发者做了很多ai插件，且不说相关插件不少需要付费，装上之后体验也比较割裂。 现在也有很多 AI 工具能很方便地解读论文，但它们和原文是分开的，读到一半想对照原文，还得来回切换。 另外做调研时，常常需要先在浏览器里快速看一批论文，再决定哪些值得收进文献库，而浏览器自带的 PDF 阅读器只能看。 所以我做了一个在浏览器里运行、原生就是围绕大模型设计的阅读器，它提供各种 AI 能力，但始终以论文为中心，AI 不会喧宾夺主：翻译、解释和回答都贴着原文出现，随时可以对照。 主要功能 论文网站一键打开，自动生成概览（总结、关键词、研究问题、方法等，内容可自定义） 按页对照翻译，划选翻译；支持大模型和机器翻译，谷歌翻译可免费使用 划选解释、划选提问、框选图片提问，回答标注原文出处 自动识别公式、表格和图片，公式可复制为 LaTeX，表格可复制为 Markdown 或 Excel 高亮、批注、Markdown 笔记 文献库支持多级文件夹和标签，可通过 WebDAV 多端同步，可与 Zotero 互相导入导出，尽量保留批注和目录结构 内置主流模型服务商，也可添加任意兼容 OpenAI 格式的接口；每个功能可以单独指定模型 数据保存在浏览器本地或自己的Webdav服务器，没有服务器；API 密钥只保存在本机。 使用 插件刚做好还没有上架商店，目前需要从 Release 下载后以「开发者模式」加载。AI 相关功能需要自备模型 API。

projects.title: Show HN: Globalize.now – translations that land in your pull request
projects.author: artursvonda
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Arturs, cofounder of globalize.now. Our view is that the best developer tools don't ask teams to change how they work. They show up where the work already happens. Dependabot doesn't make you log into a dependency dashboard; it opens a PR. Localization mostly works the other way. A TMS brings its own dashboard, upload and download loops, review queues, and a sync step someone has to own. Liam and I spent years at Lokalise watching teams reshape their process around that. It fits a localization department. It doesn't fit a small team shipping daily. So we built translation into the PR itself. Connect your GitHub repo, open a PR as usual, and we translate the new or changed strings, run QA checks, and commit the locale files to that same PR. The feature and its translations get reviewed and merged together, so nothing ships half-translated. If you'd rather keep translations separate, pick a branch instead: every push to it gets its own translation PR. Either way, files stay in your repo in your library's own format, so there's nothing to sync and nothing to migrate off. This can look trivial. A GitHub Action that sends changed strings to an LLM is an afternoon's work, and plenty of you have built one. The afternoon version is where it starts, though. Keeping terminology consistent, not re-translating what hasn't changed, catching broken placeholders and plural forms, and not paying for the whole catalog on every push is the part that keeps needing attention. We'd rather own that so you don't have to. Glossaries, style guides and translation memory are built in, and they push the output toward what a good localization team would produce. We run it on our own site, which is mostly long-form content (blog posts). Adding Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese (about 5,600 strings each) took 8 minutes and cost €31. If your app isn't i18n-ready yet, an agent skill sets up the library, extracts hardcoded strings and connects the repo: npx skills add globalize-now/globalize-skills Pricing starts at €5/month plus usage ~€0.15/1000 chars depending on size of glossary, style guide etc. No seats. We think this "tool in the middle" pattern applies well beyond translation (e.g. accessibility fixes, docs drift, language consistency). We'd like to hear where you think it breaks down, and how it works for you in practice. Try it at https://globalize.now .

projects.title: AI 错题本
projects.author: flysic
projects.summary: ## 一、为什么做这个 家里孩子上初中，数学练习册、试卷源源不断。错题管理的传统流程是：抄题（费时）、贴卷子（凌乱）、复习时东翻西找。市面上拍照搜题 App 只给答案，不管"这道题我错在哪、下次还会不会错"。 我想要的是一个**私有错题知识库**： * 拍照就能把整页题目数字化，我来审核哪些值得入库、错因是什么 * 平时能刷题、能按知识点出卷 * 连对 3 次的题自动建议归档——真正掌握的题不再占用注意力 * 数据在我自己手里 恰好此前我做过一个出题系统（ quiz-demo ），里面有一条经过实战验证的"质量链"：几何图形数值校验（ geocheck ）→ 独立解题验伪（ verify\_answers ）→ 矢量试卷导出（ export\_paper ）。错题本直接把这条链复用过来——**所有 AI 生成的题目都必须过三道工序，禁止裸奔**。 ## 二、完整工作流 拍照上传（可多张） → 视觉模型多题转录（题干 LaTeX 、选项、图形框、印刷答案、手写标记） → 自动按框抓取原图（权威图形，0 token ） → [人审视图] 左原图右题目卡片，KaTeX 实时渲染 勾选入库 + 标错因（马虎/不会/其他）+ 图形可抓原图/手动框选 年级、知识点自动归类（教材知识树），可改 → 提交入库：题库查重 → 独立解题验伪 → 章节难度知识点分析 → 工作台（筛选/统计/详情） → 刷题（单题循环，自动评分）/ 做题（勾选试卷式，统一批改给分+评价） → 连对 3 次 → 建议归档 → 归档 → 针对性出卷（按章节/知识点/难度占比，原题变式或原创）→ 矢量 PDF ## 三、功能清单（ V1.0 ） ### 1. 录入·排版机（最花功夫的模块） * **多题转录**：一张照片里所有题目一次转录，只认印刷体，手写痕迹只标记不转录 * **人审前置**：转录结果必须经人审（左原图、右题目卡片对照），勾选才入库——AI 只打草稿，取舍由人 * **图形来源分层**：几何题可一键生成规范矢量 SVG （ geocheck 数值校验循环）；默认使用原题照片裁剪图（省 token ）；表格/函数图象类题只能用原图 * **图形纠正三入口**：重新抓取原图、手动拖拽框选（ box 存档可重放）、整单幂等重裁 * **EXIF 方向统一**：手机照片的旋转信息曾导致抓图转 90°、手动框选完全错位——全链路统一到"转正空间"后彻底解决 * **年级/知识点自动归类**：教材（浙教版八上）用 build\_kb 视觉转录成知识库（ 201 页），录入时 LLM 只能在知识树内选，人审可调 ### 2. 入库质量链 * **查重**：题干归一化（去 LaTeX 命令名/标点/空白）后相似度 ≥92% 判重复，不重复录入，完成横幅里报告 * **不信任照片答案**：照片里的印刷答案仅作参考，一律让另一个模型独立解题对账；冲突以审题答案为准并留痕，判题不合格进 needs\_review * **错因驱动分析**：马虎 → 易错点写"易算错环节"；不会 → 写"思路卡点" ### 3. 工作台 * 统计图（总/在库/已归档/零练习/建议归档）+ 五组分布图（默认折叠，点开查看） * 错题列表：公式渲染、章节/难度/知识点/错因列、**查看弹窗**（题目全部信息+逐次练习历史） * **筛选联动**：章节/难度/错因/知识点/含已归档，搜索后统计和列表一起更新；筛选与勾选持久化，跨标签页不丢 * 行内归档/激活，勾选后可直接导出练习卷 PDF （矢量公式排版，答案附卷末可裁） ### 4. 刷题与做题（两种模式） * **刷题**（单题模式）：自动循环在库全部题目；单选/多选/填空**自动评分**，问答看答案自判；答完即时反馈连对 n/3 、建议归档、重复做错，可做相似题 * **做题**（试卷模式）：工作台勾选 → 新标签页整卷作答 → 统一批改：得分（百分制）、评价、**错题知识点汇总**（直指薄弱点） * **相似题**：围绕同一知识点与易错点生成，过图形校验 + 验伪，不过关自动重生成 ### 5. 多用户 按用户分目录存储（题库/草稿单/照片各自独立），页头切换/新建用户，存量数据自动迁移。两个孩子的错题互不干扰。 ## 四、几个关键设计决策 **1. 数据即文件，不用 SQLite** 全部数据是 JSON （原子写 + .bak ），人类可读、git 可版本管理（题库本身就是重要资产）。几百题规模下，一个 `git log` 就是完整的演进史——后来一次测试事故把题库覆盖了，正是靠备份和 git 恢复的。 **2. 向量化（ SVG 生成）从默认改为按需** 最初设计是"几何题都自动转成规范矢量图"，但实测发现这是**全链路最费 token 、最慢的一步**（每题 1\~3 次 LLM 调用 + geocheck 失败重试）。v0.6 反转为：转录默认用照片裁剪图（ 0 token ），需要规范图形时人审期一键生成。省一半以上开销，录入速度大幅提升。 **3. 不让 LLM 自由发挥知识点** 知识点候选来自教材知识库（把纸质课本逐页视觉转录成结构化 JSON ），录入时 LLM 只能在树内选；而**工作台筛选用的知识点候选来自题库实际标注**——保证下拉框里选了就一定能搜到（教材命名和 LLM 标注命名对不上是真实的坑）。 **4. 人审是产品的核心，不是过渡方案** 照片转录的不确定性（多题混排、手写干扰、印刷质量）决定了全自动入库不可靠。与其追求"全自动"，不如把人审界面做到顺手：对照原图逐题确认、错因标注、图形纠正都是两次点击内的事。AI 负责 80% 的体力活，人负责 20% 的判断。 ## 五、踩坑记录（节选） * **CV 定位图形在真实照片上失效**：行剖面定位在假照片上 IoU 95.9%，真实照片上把斜排文字误判为图形，两轮实测后废弃，改用视觉模型直接输出图形框 * **DeepSeek 思考链烧光 max\_tokens**：导致 content 为空且 finish\_reason=length——降级策略：json\_object → 关思考重试 → plain ，实测 645s → 16s * **EXIF orientation 双坐标系**：浏览器自动转正、服务端不转，抓图转 90°、手动框选完全错位。全链路统一转正空间 + 历史数据迁移工具 * **公式在列表里时渲染时不渲染**：题干截断 40 字符会把 `$...$` 配对切断，KaTeX 找不到闭合符就放弃——改返回全文 + CSS 单行截断 * **导出 PDF 显示 LaTeX 源码**：导出链路不渲染 LaTeX ，加了一层 LaTeX → Unicode 数学符号转换（\triangle→△、\circ→°、\frac→(a/b)、上标转 ⁰¹²³） * **测试覆盖了真实题库**：测试 patch 路径常量但存储层重构后路径被重新绑定，种子数据覆盖了真实数据（ 10 题 → 1 题）——靠 .bak 和 git 恢复，并给所有测试加了测试模式保险。这个事故再次证明了"数据即文件 + git 管理"的价值 ## 六、后续计划 * 归档题的周期性复习提醒（错题本变复习系统） * 移动端适配（拍照场景天然在手机） * 教材 KB 扩展到九年级，知识点归一化到教材命名 * 错因/知识点的长期趋势分析 ## 结语 这个项目最大的感受：**AI 应用的价值不在模型本身，而在模型外围的工程**——质量链、人审流程、数据管理、测试回归，这些"笨功夫"决定了它能不能真的每天用。3 天开发 + 真实使用反馈驱动的 12 轮迭代，现在它已经是我家每天在用的工具了。 *** *项目为自用工具，未开源服务端部署；如对质量链（ geocheck / verify\_answers / export\_paper ）或错题本实现细节感兴趣，欢迎交流。*

projects.summary: 项目发起者自荐。拾流是基于 Python 的 Windows 本机视频下载工具，使用浏览器作为操作界面。它根据链接选择专用站点适配或通用提取流程，再调用 HLS 下载器、yt-dlp 与 FFmpeg 完成下载和合并，提供队列、进度、历史记录、取消与失败重试，适合希望集中管理下载任务、减少手写命令的用户。 亮点 按站点分开维护处理步骤：同一个输入框接受作品链接或分享文案，已适配站点使用各自的路由，其他网页尝试通用提取和浏览器检测。专用适配与通用工具可以共同工作。 把任务处理过程留在本机：下载、音视频合并、任务记录和使用者主动保存的账号会话均由使用者自己的电脑管理。网页工作台可查看进度、取消任务、检查失败原因和重试。 可了解一次下载任务如何完成：项目包含站点支持矩阵、中英文说明和本地操作演示，便于查看链接识别、资源提取、下载及合并之间的分工。 解析和下载可以分别运行：实验入口可将解析结果导出为小型 JSON 任务，再由本机下载。资源可能绑定 IP、Cookie 或请求头，需要重新解析；当前仍是本地实验功能。 验证边界写清楚：公开源码曾在独立目录、全新 Python 依赖下通过 59 项自动检查，并下载、完整解码过一段匿名 1080p 短视频；仍使用已有系统工具，未声称通过所有网站或全新 Windows 系统验证。 当前已验证环境为 Windows 64 位、Python 3.13，需要 Chrome、Node.js、FFmpeg/FFprobe。界面为中文，文档提供中文和英文。多个地址的解析目前仍按顺序处理。最希望收集首次安装是否顺利、任务失败提示是否足够明确的反馈。 本机下载仍会请求来源站点及第三方服务；其中 X 的公开解析后备会把帖子编号发送给 xunlangbot.com。仅下载本人拥有或有权下载的内容，不解除 DRM 或补充缺失的访问权限。 原创代码使用 MIT 许可证，第三方组件遵守各自许可。项目及这份投稿使用 ChatGPT/Codex 协助迭代与整理；这里以项目发起者身份自荐。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】ai-token-checkin-workers：国内主流 AI 编程助手每日额度关机自动代领套件
projects.author: DewellNaa

github.name: DewellNaa/ai-token-checkin-workers
github.description: 国内主流 AI 编程助手每日额度自动签到套件（Cloudflare Worker Serverless 免开机版）

projects.summary: 国内主流 AI 编程助手每日额度自动签到套件（Cloudflare Worker Serverless 版）。电脑关机也能准时自动代领、令牌自动轮换、飞书告警卡片。 解决的痛点 国内主流 AI 编程助手（海螺 MiniMax、字节 Trae、腾讯 WorkBuddy、Qoder）每天赠送大量代码模型额度，但每天肉身把 4~5 个桌面客户端全打开一遍极其繁琐，漏打一天连签中断更是肉疼。 网上大部分签到脚本要么依赖本地常驻开机跑 Python，要么依赖三方未开源服务。为了实现「0 成本、电脑关机也能准时领、无感令牌轮换」，花时间逆向了各家的协议，写了这套基于 Cloudflare Workers 的开源套件。 核心技术特色 1. 完全 Serverless，电脑关机准时打卡：所有打卡任务直接跑在 Cloudflare Workers 免费边缘网络上，通过 Cron 定时触发，不消耗本机任何资源； 2. 令牌自洽与防风控： MiniMax Code (海螺)：基于 RFC 8628 OAuth 2.0 设备授权机制，在 Worker KV 内部单向轮换刷新 Refresh Token，一次授权终身代领； Trae CN (字节)：本地 AES-128 凭据解密与 x-device-id 设备指纹绑定，云端准时打卡； WorkBuddy (腾讯)：30 天超长 Access Token 缓存防抢占下线，同时支持自动派遣萌猫旅行出发与领取旅行特产； Qoder CN：Windows 原生 DPAPI+CNG 凭据提取，支持云端约 16 天无感容灾打卡。 3. 飞书交互卡片告警（静默模式）： 日常代领成功静默入库，不发骚扰通知；只有在 Token 过期或接口变动时，才会向飞书群/私聊推送红色预警交互卡片。 4. 跨平台一键状态巡检： 提供跨平台 python checkall.py 与 PowerShell 原生脚本，一键秒级查看所有平台打卡状态、连签天数与最新积分。 开源遵循 MIT 协议，年化相当于免费获取价值超过 ¥1,200+ 的商业大模型推理额度。希望对经常使用国内 AI 编程助手的开发者有所帮助！

projects.title: 🚀我在安卓设备上复刻了豆包手机功能！最懂你的安卓 AI 助手 Kitten 来了！
projects.author: WJZ0821
projects.summary: # [Kitten 项目地址(点我！！！)]( https://github.com/WJZ-P/Kitten) ![image|565x500]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJZ-P/Kitten/main/markdown/banner.webp) ## 前言 大家肯定都或多或少听说过豆包手机的魔力：跟 AI 说一句话，豆包自动在后台帮你打开 APP ，并操作应用。但必须购买他们的努比亚定制豆包手机才能玩起来，现在我做了一个 Kitten 助手，利用特权进程+无障碍权限完美复刻了豆包手机的核心功能：在副屏操纵 APP ，无需用户操心。 给大家简单看下 UI 界面。 ![1]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJZ-P/Kitten/main/markdown/screenshot-chat.webp) ![2]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJZ-P/Kitten/main/markdown/screenshot-tokens.webp) 上图是一个测试用例，目前是已经执行完任务了的结果，正在执行任务时，副屏会在卡片的右侧显示，并且支持点击放大，让你可以看到 AI 是怎么操控你的 APP 的。 UI 设计上参考了 ios 的液态玻璃，使用了安卓侧的一个开源液态玻璃实现，在输入框和底部 tab 、设置的开关中均可体验到丝滑的液态玻璃效果。 目前项目只是测试版，还有很多不足之处，API Key 这些需要大家手动输入，市面上的 AI 基本都支持。 ## 技术细节 使用 APP 需要先开启开发者模式，软件会监听无线调试服务，得现在手机的无线调试中配对上，才能够使得 Kitten 拥有能够拉起副屏的特权进程，这是必要的。并且代码完全开源，没有任何后台偷偷上传的动作，大家可以放心使用~ 具体的屏幕识别，会优先使用无障碍服务获取页面节点，如果 AI 觉得有必要的话就会调用截图，获取副屏当前画面内容来辅助判断。 ## 感谢大家~ 更多细节就放在 GitHub 的 README 主页里了，就不再赘述，希望大家多多评论，多多 star🌟~

projects.title: 【工具自荐】GIFGenerator.ai：通过文字或图片，使用 AI 生成 GIF 动图
projects.author: gifgenerator
projects.summary: GIFGenerator.ai：让静态图片动起来的 AI GIF 生成工具 大家好，最近开发并上线了一个 AI GIF 动图生成工具 —— GIFGenerator.ai。 项目的想法来源于一个很简单的问题：现在 AI 已经能够生成各种精美的图片，但如果想让这些图片动起来，制作成可以循环播放的 GIF 动图，往往还需要额外的动画工具和编辑流程。 传统制作 GIF 的方式通常需要准备多张图片、制作逐帧动画，或者先生成视频，再通过其他工具转换为 GIF。对于只想快速制作一个表情包、动态插画、网站动画素材的普通用户来说，这个过程有些繁琐。 因此，我做了 AI GIF Generator，希望把 GIF 动画的创作过程简化为：输入描述或上传图片 → AI 生成动画 → 获取 GIF 动图。 不需要学习 Photoshop、After Effects 等专业软件，也不需要手动绘制每一帧，就可以尝试把一个简单的创意转换成动态内容。 ✨ 主要功能 1. Text to GIF：通过文字描述生成 GIF 只需要用自然语言描述自己想要的动画内容，AI 就可以根据描述生成相应的 GIF 动图。 例如： 一只橘猫坐在窗边，慢慢摇晃尾巴。 一个像素风格的小机器人在草地上行走。 一颗卡通爱心有节奏地跳动，形成循环动画。 一只戴着墨镜的柴犬踩着滑板向前滑行。 一个可爱的 3D 卡通角色向镜头挥手。 对于没有动画制作经验的用户来说，只需要描述场景、角色、动作和风格，就能够快速尝试不同的动画创意。 2. Image to GIF：让静态图片变成动态 GIF 除了文字生成，还支持通过上传图片来创建动画。 比如你已经有一张 AI 生成的插画、宠物照片、卡通角色或者 Logo，可以直接上传图片，并通过文字描述希望添加的运动效果。 一些典型的使用方式： 照片动画化：让照片中的猫咪眨眼、转头，或做出简单的动作。 插画动画化：让插画中的人物挥手、微笑，或者让画面中的元素产生动态效果。 Logo 动画：让静态品牌 Logo 旋转、缩放、移动或产生简单的循环效果。 角色动画：让原创卡通人物跳跃、行走、挥手，制作动态角色素材。 表情包制作：将一张有趣的图片转换成适合聊天分享的动态 GIF。 这种方式比较适合已经有现成图片，希望在保留原始视觉元素的基础上增加动画效果的用户。 3. 支持不同风格的 GIF 动画创作 GIF 不只是传统的聊天表情包，也可以用于 UI 动画、视觉设计、创意展示和网站内容。 GIFGenerator.ai 可以用于尝试不同类型的动画，例如： Pixel Art GIF：复古像素风格动画，适合游戏角色、像素场景和怀旧风格内容。 Cartoon GIF：卡通角色、可爱表情和轻松有趣的动画。 3D Animation GIF：3D 卡通人物、玩具风格角色以及简单的动态展示。 Anime GIF：动漫插画风格的动态创作。 Looping GIF：适合在网页、社交媒体和聊天工具中重复播放的循环动画。 通过描述不同的视觉风格、动作和场景，可以快速探索不同的动画效果。 4. 使用自然语言控制动画效果 除了描述画面内容，还可以在提示词中指定动画的运动方式。 例如： 一只手绘风格的猫头鹰站在树枝上，缓慢眨眼并轻轻歪头。镜头保持固定，背景不变，动作自然，最后回到初始姿势，形成平滑循环。 相比手动制作关键帧，这种方式降低了动画创作的门槛。 对于有明确需求的创作者，还可以在描述中添加运动方向、动作节奏、视觉风格和循环效果等细节。 需要说明的是，AI 生成结果存在一定的随机性，复杂动作和精确的循环衔接可能需要多次调整提示词。 🎯 适合哪些使用场景？ 1. 社交媒体和表情包创作 可以用来制作聊天表情包、社交平台动态图片、趣味角色动画等，让原本静态的内容更加生动。 2. 网站和产品设计 开发者和设计师可以尝试使用 AI GIF 制作网站上的简单动态插画、产品展示素材、加载动画或其他视觉元素。 3. 独立开发者的产品宣传 对于没有专职设计师的独立开发者，可以通过简单的文字描述，为自己的 SaaS 产品、应用介绍或社交媒体宣传制作动态素材。 4. 插画师和内容创作者 已有插画作品的创作者，可以尝试让静态作品增加眨眼、挥手、头发飘动等简单动画效果，探索新的内容展示方式。 5. 宠物和生活照片创作 上传宠物照片或其他有趣的图片，通过 AI 添加动作，制作适合分享给朋友的个性化 GIF。 🚀 如何使用？ 整个使用流程比较简单： 1. 打开 GIFGenerator.ai 网站。 2. 选择文字生成 GIF，或者上传一张想要制作动画的图片。 3. 输入动画描述，说明角色应该如何运动、希望呈现什么风格。 4. 提交生成任务，等待 AI 处理。 5. 预览生成结果，并获取需要的 GIF 动图。 例如，上传一张原创卡通角色图片，输入： 让这个角色开心地跳起来，双手举高，落地后轻轻弹跳，镜头固定，背景保持不变，制作成流畅的循环 GIF。 就可以尝试把静态角色转换成动态形象。 🌐 项目地址 英文首页：GIFGenerator.ai - AI GIF Generator 中文首页：AI GIF 生成器 - 在线制作 GIF 动图 💡 为什么做这个项目？ 现在 AI 图片生成工具已经很多，但是制作 GIF 动画仍然有一些使用门槛。 有些工具偏向专业的视频生成，操作复杂；有些工具只能把已有视频转换成 GIF，并不能直接根据文字或图片生成动画。 我希望 GIFGenerator.ai 能够更专注于 GIF 动图这个使用场景，让用户不必为了制作一个几秒钟的动画，去学习复杂的软件或者经过多个工具的转换流程。 项目目前仍在持续完善中，后续也希望根据实际反馈改善动画生成效果、创作流程以及 GIF 的使用体验。 如果大家平时有制作 GIF 表情包、网站动态素材、角色动画的需求，欢迎体验并提出建议。 也很想了解大家在实际使用 AI 生成 GIF 时遇到的问题，例如角色一致性、动作自然度、循环衔接效果等。 感谢阮老师和《科技爱好者周刊》提供分享项目的平台！

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source customer-facing agents
projects.author: zualas
projects.summary: Hi, Dmitri from Radioso here, an open-source platform to design AI agents for customers and visitors in any channel, in the style of Fin/Ada/Decagon. The repo is https://github.com/radioso-ai/radioso and our website is https://radioso.ai Today, your choices are: 1. Buy a very expensive service for your vertical (usually starting with $$ five figures monthly) 2. Get a cheap off-the-shelf chatbot that mostly answers FAQs 3. Build your own, and then also build the inbox, human handoff, audit trail and integrations around it At Radioso we wanted an open-source option that combines the best of all 3. You can integrate it with your own software via API/SDK or your CRM, or run it standalone, either self-hosted or in our cloud. The engine runs multi-step interactions and takes actions: calling your APIs, updating records, booking things. Maybe you’ve tried Parlant; Radioso is the alternative “with batteries included”: RAG, audit trail, customer service inbox, and integrations like Slack and email. Under the hood it’s plain TypeScript + PostgreSQL, works with OpenAI/Anthropic/other models, and is licensed under Apache 2.0 which includes all features (The only thing we keep under EE license is the multi-tenant layer we use to run our own cloud). We have existing customers running it for technical Q&A, course booking, online product recommendations and goods returns, among others, some reaching 92% of conversations automated. We’re currently working on voice support so we can offer a call center. Our ambition is to be “the WordPress of customer-facing AI” :), where people can contribute their favorite plugins and benefit from the ecosystem. Longer term, we think browsing the web will mostly mean talking to your own agent, and when you need a service or a purchase, your agent will talk to the vendor’s agent to get things done. For this, Radioso already publishes an A2A Agent Card and we’re working on the rest. Your Radioso services are also callable over MCP, for customers who already use it. Thanks for your attention. We’d especially love to hear which integrations you’d want, whether you’d self-host it, and what’s stopped you from deploying a customer-facing AI agent so far. Tell us what you think.

projects.summary: 这是一个运行在 Android 手机上的 AI 智能体，用一句话描述任务（比如“打开设置，告诉我电量”），它就会截图读屏，自己点击、滑动、输入，直到完成。不需要电脑和 adb，只有调用大模型时联网，支持 OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic 和本地 Ollama 模型。适合用来学习手机 GUI 智能体的原理和 Android 无障碍服务开发。 亮点 完全在手机上运行：通过无障碍服务截图、读取界面元素并执行操作，不依赖电脑或 adb 连接。 定位方式稳：优先按界面元素编号点击，找不到时再用 0-1000 归一化坐标，兼容自绘界面。 过程透明：悬浮球实时显示每一步，任务记录保存每一步的截图、动作、推理、耗时和 tokens，还有每步耗时图。 注重隐私：API Key 用 Android Keystore 加密，Base URL 默认隐藏，报错信息里的服务器地址也会脱敏。 中英文界面，可选离线语音唤醒（说“你好阿特”）。 参考 Google 开源的 ARTEMIS 设计，用 Java 移植到手机端，代码适合学习研究。

github.name: ImpossibleComputing/jacq
github.description: Jacq inference compiler and CUDA kernel DSL

projects.summary: I was working (with agents) on testing out various attention algorithm ideas I had, and I found that the existing infrastructure/libraries made it more difficult than it should be. So I created Jacq, a DSL and compiler. A jacq file describes a model’s configuration, weights, layers, and pipeline. Jacq turns it into a standalone CUDA inference runtime and a Python weight exporter. Kernel descriptions can also generate CUDA harnesses. The easiest way to try it is the TinyLlama example in the README. Building, validating, visualizing, and generating CUDA only require Rust. Of course, running inference does require an NVIDIA GPU, CUDA, Python dependencies, and weights. Jacq doesn't support other GPU vendors (AMD, etc) or Metal, yet (PR's welcome!) There's also an experimental vLLM patch to compile and patch your jacq file into a vLLM build, as well. Feedback very welcome!

projects.title: X/twitter 运营必用 Skill, 可以审查发帖, 也可以问问题
projects.author: liyu7352
projects.summary: 前段时间研究了一轮 X / Twitter 的公开推荐代码，整理成了文章。后来发现，这些内容更适合做成一个可以随时提问的工具：碰到具体问题，直接查对应的代码和适用条件。 于是做了 **For You Skills**，给 Claude Code 、Codex 、Cursor 等支持 Skills 的工具使用。 项目：[github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills) 如果你也在经营 X ，可能纠结过这些问题： - 今天已经发了一篇，另一篇要不要等到明天？ - 一篇长文，应该发普通 Post 、Thread ，还是 Article ？ - 网上说“第二篇曝光打六折”，这个说法到底从哪来的？ - 草稿写好了，开头、长度和配图有什么具体问题？ 这些都可以直接问它。 我比较在意的是**回答的依据能不能查到**。所以除了研究结论，也把对应的原始代码链接、适用条件和未解决的问题整理进了知识库。回答时会查相关条目，再给建议；公开证据不足的地方，也要说明白。 比如“第二篇打六折”这个案例，重点就是查清楚代码里的“第二篇”到底在数什么，以及分数倍率能不能直接理解成曝光比例。演示里保留了这次问答和对应源码，可以自己核对。 有草稿的话，也可以让它审稿。它会检查实际开头、统计长度、考虑首图和后续配图、判断内容更适合哪种发布形式，并给出具体修改。目前一共 8 个技能，通过一个总入口按问题选择工作流。 安装先用这一条： ```bash npx skills add alexliyu7352/for-you-skills --skill x-assistant ``` 装好后，可以在对应工具里试着问： > 使用 x-assistant：我今天上午已经发了一篇 X 帖子，下午还有一篇不同主题的内容。该今天发还是明天发？请给建议，并说明相关源码支持什么、不能证明什么。 也说明一下边界：知识库基于特定版本的公开源码研究，不能据此确认全部线上配置，也不能保证涨粉或曝光。模型、联网和生图等能力由你使用的工具提供。 这里有 [78 秒案例演示及完整记录]( https://github.com/alexliyu7352/for-you-skills/tree/main/docs/demo)，之前的 [中文研究文章]( https://blog.go5.si/posts/zh/x-algorithm-teardown/) 也保留着。 想找一些本身就在用 AI 工具、也有 X 发帖需求的人试试。尤其欢迎拿你真正纠结过的问题，或者一篇准备发布的草稿来测试。 如果试了，最想听到的是：**它有没有帮你做出一个具体决定？哪一段回答仍然空泛，或者证据对不上？**

projects.title: 【资源自荐】从 microGPT 到唐诗 GPT：中文动手课，包含训练、生成和失败实验
projects.author: OakcoderX

github.name: OakcoderX/TangShiGPT-Course
github.description: 从 microGPT 到唐诗 GPT：原始《全唐诗》、可运行代码、HTML 与 PPT 教案，以及真实的李白风格实验。

projects.summary: 自荐一套面向会一点 Python 的初学者的中文动手课：从 microGPT 到唐诗 GPT。 课程受 Karpathy 的 microgpt 启发，采用独立的 PyTorch 教学实现，带学习者把《全唐诗》JSON 整理成字符序列，训练、保存、加载一个小 GPT，再观察它怎样生成五言、七言形式的草稿。 学习路径包括： 先做“下一字频数”基线，再训练模型，比较统计规律与模型输出。 从小规模短跑开始，练习保存权重和继续训练。 用真实的李白风格实验学习设计对照、匿名比较输出和判断失败。当前模型能生成唐诗形式的草稿，但李白风格仍不能稳定复现。 完整学习包提供 HTML 自学教案、可编辑 PPTX、代码、语料、权重和实验记录。下载解压后，用浏览器打开 docs/index.html 阅读教案；运行代码需要 Python 3.10 以上和项目依赖，支持 CPU，亦可尝试 CUDA 或 Apple MPS。 这是公开免费学习项目，不是 Karpathy 的官方课程。自有代码、教案和权重目前没有附开源许可证，上游数据许可已在包内保留。欢迎反馈最难跟上的步骤。

projects.title: Show HN: stardelt.io – a self-hosted lakehouse on k8s (pre-alpha)
projects.author: schwarztrinker
projects.summary: I am pretty honest: there are a ton of vibecoded projects around, and I made another one... great huh? I'm working as a data platform engineer in Germany. My day job is basically spinning up & running lakehouse platforms on US hyperscalers for SMB and some DAX companies. I mean, data engineers like to work on these platforms but since some time I really have ethical concerns about it - like: - vendor lock-in - high costs (because of cloud costs - and in most cases you are not able to connect your own metal if you have one) - non-EU vendors... - other open-source solutions have high license costs for LDAP etc. pp. That's why is started to build my own opinionated data lakehouse platform in my spare time (tbh I also started learning agentic engineering and what harnesses are..), only curated from open source projects already available. The building blocks are pretty straightforward imo: - Iceberg tables on whatever S3 storage you already have - Trino for SQL and Spark Connect for jobs - Airflow for schedules, plus notebooks, Kafka streams and dashboards - One web UI and one API over all of it - stuff around like OIDC, secrets management etc. It's fully pre-alpha. But I want to use it as an internal pitch project at my current employer to push agentic engineering & the idea of creating our own data platform for our non-hyperscaler customers. Site: https://stardelt.io Code: https://github.com/stardelt I'm happy to hear what you think about it :) Cheers, Martin

projects.title: Herdr 的终端界面能把事情做好。Shepi 让你在 Mac 上用得更愉快。
projects.author: wisteen
projects.summary: 同时让几个 AI 编程 agent 做事，难点不只在于怎么给任务。一个在本机改接口，一个在检查测试，服务器上还有一个处理数据。你得不断切回终端，确认谁还在工作，谁正等着你。 我做的 [Shepi]( https://shepi.app/?v=20261107)，是 Herdr 的原生 Mac 客户端，与 Herdr TUI 实时共享同一套工作空间、标签页和 agents ，并支持简体中文、英文和日文。它不是另建一份桌面会话，也不需要你迁移现有工作。Herdr 负责维持 AI 编程 agent 的终端会话，Shepi 提供桌面入口，让任务、进度、产物和需要你参与的时刻，都有清楚的位置。 ## 01 · 现有的终端会话，打开就在那里 Shepi 和 Herdr TUI 连接同一个 Herdr server ，实时共享同一套工作空间、标签页和 agents 。在终端启动的会话，会直接出现在 Shepi ；从 Shepi 启动的，也能在终端里看到。两端可以同时使用，不用迁移，不是复制一份，也不会为桌面界面另开一套独立会话。 Claude Code 、Codex 、OpenCode 、Gemini CLI 、Cursor 、Copilot CLI ，仍然运行在完整的真实终端里。旋转标记表示工作中，空心圆表示空闲，状态也有文字；当前输入的窗格是更浅的卡片。想用桌面窗口就打开，想回 TUI 就回去，接着做的是同一份工作。 ![Shepi 窗口：左侧是工作区和 agent 的边栏，顶部是标签页，中间是三个窗格，底部是状态栏。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/window.webp) *工作区、agent 状态和真实终端，在同一个窗口里。（指南原图）* ## 02 · 需要你时，不必靠反复巡视发现 当 agent 停下来请求确认，例如准备部署、删除或安装时，侧栏、窗格标题和状态栏会亮起琥珀色； agent 提供操作信息时，也能看见它要执行什么。收起侧栏仍有横幅，切到其他应用会收到 macOS 通知，知道谁停了、工作了多久，点击查看就能回去。声音沿用 Herdr 的提醒时机，远程机器也一样。我希望你能专心做别的事，而不是守着输出等待。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/needs.mp4) ## 03 · 把背景和选项讲清楚，再请你决定 在你要求时，agent 可以发来带背景、选项及各自后果的提问卡。你从任何窗格都能点选，或写自己的回答，答案直接回给对应 agent 。它也能打开网页、在名称下报告进度，或在自身上下左右打开测试和日志窗格，标明归属而不抢键盘焦点；远程 agent 同样可用。这些动作让确认与检查留在工作旁边，不必从长段输出里寻找入口。 ![claude 问 “Deploy to staging?”，卡片位于窗口右上角，写明了情况，有三个回答，每个都说明会做什么，Deploy 标为“建议”，还有一个可以自己写回答的输入框； claude 窗格泛着琥珀色光。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/ask.webp) *先了解情况，再选择下一步；也可以直接写自己的回答。（指南原图）* ## 04 · 一项工作结束，把下一项交接清楚 有些任务适合分段完成。前一个 agent 做完后，可以留下交接提示，结束当前窗格，再由一个新的 agent 在同一位置接手。也可以安排稍后开始，或等另一个 agent 完成后再执行。安排在机器上运行，关闭 Shepi 也会继续；需要你介入时，仍然停下来等待。我想提供的是清楚的接续位置，而不是假设开发过程不再需要人判断。 ## 05 · 回来时，知道它进行到哪一步 一句“还在工作”，不足以解释任务的进展。Agent 可以把计划放在 Shepi 里，当前步骤显示在名称下面，状态旁有累计工作时长。把指针停在步骤上或点击，就能展开全部步骤、进度条、当前项与每一步的耗时。关掉窗口再打开，这些进度仍然保留。回来时可以先读清位置，再决定是否需要翻完整输出。 ![边栏：带分支和 agent 徽标的工作区，以及显示标志、已工作时长和当前步骤的 agent ；其中一个 agent 的任务卡片在旁边打开，进行到第 3 步（共 4 步）。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/agents.webp) *当前步骤留在侧栏，完整计划和耗时可以展开查看。（指南原图）* ## 06 · 不只听“完成了”，也看看实际改动 检查结果时，我希望能顺手对照代码，而不只是读 agent 的总结。Shepi 可以查看本机和远程项目自上次提交以来的未提交变更。通过状态栏，或 prefix 后按 d 打开 diff ，按习惯选择并排或单列阅读；看完按 Esc ，就回到原来的窗格。这里做的是查看，不负责暂存或编辑代码，把后续操作留给你自己的工作流程。 ![差异视图：左侧是更改的文件，右侧是更改内容。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/diff.webp) *把 agent 的说明与实际变更对照着看。（指南原图）* ## 07 · 远程机器，加入同一个工作视野 如果任务跑在服务器上，可以直接在 Shepi 内添加 SSH 机器，使用已有的密钥。输入主机后，由 Herdr 连接；机器会以自己的标题加入侧栏，下面是它的工作区和 agents 。每个工作区都有需介入、工作中、完成和空闲的数量。本机改页面、远程处理数据时，不必把机器边界变成另一套窗口管理负担。 ![窗口上方的“添加机器”表单。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/machines.webp) *从应用内添加 SSH 机器，和本机任务一起查看。（指南原图）* ## 08 · 在 agent 旁边，留一个能动手的 shell Agent 改完接口，你可能想自己跑一次测试；排查异常时，也可能需要持续看日志。Shepi 可以向旁边或下方拆分真实 shell ，让这些操作紧邻当前任务：跑测试、追踪日志，或用命令打开 PR 。新窗格在原布局中展开，不必另找一个终端窗口，也不用把自己的检查命令塞进 agent 的输入流。协作不只有观看，随时动手也应当方便。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/split.mp4) ## 09 · 输入之前，清楚自己正对着谁 几个 agent 并排时，发错位置比少看一条输出更让人分心。Shepi 用更浅的卡片标出当前输入窗格，只有这里有闪烁光标，标题也写着 agent 的名字。其他窗格保持完整亮度，不会因为失去焦点就暗下去，仍然方便对照输出。可以点击切换，也能用 prefix 加 h 、j 、k 、l 移到相邻窗格，让注意力和键盘去向保持一致。 ## 10 · 布局变零碎，一次把空间分匀 工作过程中不断拆分、拖动，窗格难免变得有大有小。有时你并不需要精确设计比例，只想让每个任务重新获得差不多的阅读空间。prefix 加 = 会让当前标签页里的窗格均分空间，无论此前怎样拆分或调整，都能把布局收拾齐整。我希望整理窗口是一个随手动作，不必在真正的任务之外，再花时间经营一套布局。 ## 11 · 把当前问题看大，也保留原来的位置 读一段长日志，或专心看一个 agent 的结果时，可以用 prefix 加 z 把当前窗格放大到整个窗口，文字保持原位。其他窗格只是留在后面，并没有被关闭；角标、标签页和窗格标题会提醒你正在缩放。再按同一个键，或点击还原，就能回到原布局。临时专注不需要先拆散工作现场，看完也不用重新排列其他任务。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/zoom.mp4) ## 12 · 重复输入，交给知道等待的宏 切换模型、重启开发服务器，或顺序输入几条命令，可以收进一个宏。它不只是连续敲字符，也能等前一步的内容出现在屏幕上再继续：例如等待模型菜单出现，再移动和确认。可以让当前 agent 编写、试运行并告诉你按键，也能让它修改、列出或删除；愿意自己写，就在 Settings 里完成。本机和远程都能用，把明确重复的动作收起来，留出判断的精力。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/macro.mp4) ## 13 · 它做出的页面，就放在旁边检查 让 agent 展示页面，网页就能在旁边打开，本机开发服务和远程服务器提供的页面都可以。你能直接点击交互，也有后退、前进、刷新和在外部浏览器打开的入口。即便光标落在网页输入框里，Shepi 的 prefix 仍然有效，按 Esc 可以把键盘操作交还窗口。检查页面和继续终端工作，不必来回寻找各自藏在哪个应用里。 ![一个 agent 在旁边的窗格中打开了它的开发服务器页面。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/web.webp) *开发服务器与页面并排，方便检查刚完成的结果。（指南原图）* ## 14 · 相关内容放近，终端继续运行 日志应该靠近正在排查问题的 agent ，测试也可以移到更方便对照的位置。拖住窗格标题，松手前就能预览布局：交换两个窗格，或放到另一个的上、下、左、右。拖到其他标签页可以跨 tab 移动，悬停后还能精确选择落点；放到加号上，就单独建立一个标签页。位置改变时，终端始终继续运行，整理现场不必打断工作。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/move.mp4) ## 15 · 记住一点线索，就能找回任务 不一定每次都记得任务在哪台机器、哪个工作区里。Shepi 的统一搜索覆盖机器、工作区、agents 、窗格和最近输出，本机与 SSH 机器都在同一个入口。输入一两个词，可以组合查询，也不必遵守固定词序，找到结果后按 Return 就能进入。无论记住的是任务名字，还是刚看过的一段输出，都可以从线索回到工作位置。 ![打开的查找，输入了查询，结果按类型分组。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/find.webp) *同一个搜索入口，同时找任务位置和输出中的线索。（指南原图）* ## 16 · 刚才的位置，不用再找一遍 有时并不需要完整搜索，只是切出去看了一眼，想回到刚才的窗格。Cmd E 会列出跨机器最近使用的位置，按最近顺序排列，并默认选中刚离开的那一个。再按 Return ，就回去了。列表也支持输入文字查找，和搜索一样使用。处理几个交错的任务时，这样的小入口能让临时切换更直接，不必每次都重新辨认侧栏和标签页。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/recent.mp4) ## 17 · 错过的事情，留在收件箱里 Shepi 开着而你离开时，不是每条通知都会当场看到。期间 agent 完成任务、需要介入或发来问题的事件，会留在查找旁边的收件箱里，Dock 也显示数量。点击其中一条，可以直达对应窗格；查看那个窗格之后，提醒才会清掉。我希望回来之后有迹可循，先接住等待处理的事情，而不是重新巡视所有终端，猜测离开时发生了什么。 ![托盘按钮下方的收件箱，列出在你没在看时需要你处理或已完成的 agent 。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/inbox.webp) *错过的事件留在这里，回来接着处理。（指南原图）* ## 18 · 关掉窗口，工作仍有自己的位置 退出 Shepi 、关掉窗口，或关闭 Herdr TUI ，都不会停止底层 server 中的 agents 。远程服务器上的任务，在这台 Mac 睡眠时也继续运行。重新打开 Shepi ，可以回到原来的工作位置；如果中间断开连接，状态栏还会告诉你有多少窗格发生了变化。窗口是入口，不是任务存在的前提，可以离开，也能在回来时接着做。 Shepi 继承 Herdr 的 prefix 和键位，默认是 Control-B ，也支持鼠标。我希望保留终端的直接，同时把多任务、远程连接与需要人参与的环节讲清楚。如果你经常同时使用几个 AI 编程 agent ，或在 Mac 与服务器之间切换，这就是我想照顾的工作场景。 整个应用支持简体中文、英文和日文，可以跟随 Mac 的语言，也可以在设置里切换，立即生效，不用重启。菜单、设置、提问卡、提示消息和通知等界面内容都有对应翻译；终端里的 agent 、命令和输出则保留原样。网站和用户指南也提供这三种语言，阅读说明与实际操作可以用同一种界面语言。 Shepi 适用于 macOS 15 及以上，支持 Apple silicon 和 Intel Mac ，需要 Herdr 0.9.3 及以上。它是我独立开发的产品，非 Herdr 官方应用。

projects.title: 【资源自荐】三组 AI 结果核对练习：交接、资料来源与代码变更
projects.author: m8500321
projects.summary: 分享三组免费的中文练习，练习给 AI 交任务后怎么核对结果。每组都有完整模拟材料、提示词和参考核对点： 任务交接：分清内部预览和对外发布，保留未确认的负责人、预算。 资料来源：不同样本、平均数与中位数为什么不能直接合并。 代码变更：需求只改按钮文案，提交却顺带改了金额舍入，应该怎样验收。 无需注册，可复制、改写和用于教学；可以人工完成，也可用自己已有的 AI 工具，模型服务费用另计。下面可直接展开一组完整练习。 由 CC-Brichy777 / CCHello 项目方使用 AI 辅助制作，全部是模拟资料，尚无人类讲师审定或课堂实测。外链页面有项目方署名、CCHello 付费第三方桌面服务说明及官网入口；练习不要求使用或推荐产品。 直接试做：把讨论整理成可交接的任务 先读下面六条模拟讨论，分清已经决定的事、暂定安排和仍需追问的问题。 材料 N01：周一讨论，演示页暂定周五发。设计同学小林先出两版首页，周三前给大家看。 N02：周二补充，周五只是内部预览，不是对外发布。公开发布日期需要等隐私说明和测试一起过。 N03：测试负责人阿青说周四可以检查登录流程；支付流程还没有安排测试负责人。 N04：大家提到预算先按2000元准备，小周追问能否提高到3000元。会上没有确认。 N05：小林说首页只保留一个主要按钮，按钮文案还没定。两版稿都不代表最终方案。 N06：会议结束前确认，内部预览前要隐藏演示数据中的邮箱和订单号。没有分配执行人。 给 AI 的任务 请只根据以上模拟材料整理交接清单。每行给出事项、状态（已确认／暂定／待确认）、材料明确写出的负责人、时间和来源编号。没有写出的信息填“未确认”，不要替参与者决定预算、日期或负责人。最后列出最先需要追问的三个问题。 拿到结果后，逐项回看原文 周五是内部预览，没有推断出公开发布日期。回看 N01、N02。 支付测试与脱敏的执行人仍待确认。回看 N03、N06。 没有把3000元写成获批预算，保留2000元准备口径与3000元提问。回看 N04。 周三前提供两版首页；最终方案和按钮文案没有确认。回看 N01、N05。 关键结论有来源编号，没有把追问写成既定事实。 保留第一版结果，再写下“已核实、需修正、待追问”各一项。这些核对点是供人工检查的参考，不是自动评分，也不保证穷尽所有问题。

projects.summary: Hi HN. I made AJX (Agent Journey Experience). It is a CLI and skill bundle that you run to test what your product feels like to use from the point of view of an agent, and you get back a list of "asks" that would improve your product from an agentic usability perspective: so that agents spend less time, tokens and retries to accomplish tasks with it. How? It works by having an outer loop (AJX harness skill + CLI) that controls an "inner loop": the agent that actually tries out your product. The outer loop investigates the inner loop once it finishes. To try it, copy the prompt from the main page into your favorite agent and it will install the skill and CLI and you can then trigger /ajx skill, give it a prompt and some simple configuration as text, and it helps you with the rest. The outer loop starts loading the configured harness of your choice (claude, codex, kiro-cli etc..) in an environment and configuration of your choice (docker, VM, local, with or without specific skills, specific model, amount of runs, and more), and provides the harness (inner loop) with your input prompt and links, and "definition of done" - what does it mean to succeed with this product? For example with vercel cli you could say "build and deploy a simple hello world with vercel CLI [link]" as the prompt for the AJX test. Once the inner loop harness runs its course, the outer harness loop examines the run, logs and details, and outputs and extract the needed information from that run: retries, tokens, mistakes, assumptions and more, and created a very detailed report, as well as a list of asks that if applied to the product, would improve the agentic journey given the same prompt in the future. I call this "Agent Journey eXperience" it's the agentic equivalent of "User Experience" - if we were to document the journey an agent does when trying your product for the first time in a specific scenario. - Where does it go astray and makes mistakes? - How many retries does it take to succeed with the task? - How much time? - How many tokens? List of ASKS as an output: What features/fixes would the agent want the product to have to save it from making these mistakes or costing extra time and token in the future? here are some examples: - CLI missing a --JSON, which cost lots of parsing of unneeded code - CLI missing commands like doctor, help aliases - DOCS disagree with behavior of the product - Skills pull the agent in the wrong direction - lack of feedback while product is executing - Human friendly CLIs outputs break the agent loop - and much more. Why? I'm a startups solutions architect @ AWS, and previously wrote the art of unit testing and did lots of work on code quality, engineering practiced and continuous delivery) I built AJX (ajx.dev) when I was tasked with giving feedback on an internal upcoming AWS product that is meant to be used by agents. The team wanted feedback from potential users, and I figured that agents are the new potential users. I figured that if I was a product owner, I'd love to know what it feels like to work with my product (CLI, SDK, Website, Docs etc), and that the harder the agents work to use my product, the less people would point their agent at it, or the less the agent would tend to recommend it. Also I think it's useful to have "brag points" that your product is "agent-friendly". I even tested AJX with AJX and it found great of issues with the CLI (for example ajx status was returning the wrong status sometimes, ajx init --task behaved differently than expected, and other cool stuff like that. I envision this being used as part of a CI/CD cycle with a loop until AJX returns "all green" and no ASKS. AJX is still very new - so probably lots of rough edges but in an agent first world, I think it's a step in the right direction: see the world from an agent's POV.

projects.title: Show HN: Jev vs. OpenAI Decision vs. Small Financial World Models: FinBench [video]
projects.author: atul-mehra
projects.summary: Guys - OpenAI Decisions, Jev, World Models are interesting. We ran some tests for the C-suite to decide between OpenAI Decisions vs. their own existing models vs. training their proprietary Financial World Model. Sharing the results of our sample tests. If you like a walkthrough with video of results - see this video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UN1LIF01uHQ We are also trying to reach OpenAI team & community to collaborate on running various tests to help the C-suite to make decisions. Which involves which business cases, they wish to map on which Decision models. Summary: Small Financial World Model compared to OpenAI Decisions. This test is not to build a better model. But to help C-suites make informed choices. There are various considerations viz Latency Cost per decision On-premises or Hosted APIs Regulatory & Compliance Mapping to use cases Financial modelling or LLM-based reasoning as underlying architecture We ran tests to: Predict credit defaults Cross-sell propensity Churn Risk Future cash flows Future state of customers & causal impacts of interventions like no-action, Payment reminders etc. These tests are specific to banking use cases. Why Benchmark & comparison: Small on-prem Decision Models are needed due to latency, cost, regulatory or protecting the proprietary data for Enterprises. This benchmarking helps C-suite executives to decide which option - their in-house models or other options are better. Vaayu FinBench also includes some specific banking-related business cases as examples. World Model also has action-conditioning. Thus, it predicts which decision optimizes the future outcomes. Eg Risk weighted return or prevent default. Core ask from Banks Small Financial World Model is trained on-premesis on proprietary data for enterprises. Scope - This is only for demonstration purposes to give a glimpse of how to compare various options. The dataset & model size is way too small yet. On a larger proprietary dataset, the results need to be benchmarked. Results: Latency - A co-located Small Financial World Model way improves latency. Major part may be coming due to network latency. So this is one area where we would like to discuss alternatives with OpenAI team & community. Is there a smaller on-premesis version for Decision Model avaialble for co-location. Credit Defaults - Our Small Financial World model worked worse than Decision API. Cash Churn & Cross Sell propensity - Our Small Financial World model improved marginally. It’s obvious that since Decision API hasnt seen the propreitary data. The marginal improvement shows model is learning..but our model is very very small (Few 100 thousand parameters) trained on small dataset.. But test demonstrates - architecture is capable of learning better. Action conditions outcomes - This is available in World Model …but we aren’t aware of this in Decision API yet. Financial Modelling - Model is trained finance native can handle temporal & causal scenarios If you like a walkthrough - see this video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UN1LIF01uHQ Disclaimer: This is quick tests results & has some know issues. This is only for demonstration purpose. We have included OpenAI Decisions for now...Including Jev in next releases. At the moment talking to C-suite & Banks for what they wish. We find Decision API & World Models interesting developments especially in finance & enterprises space. Looking forward to collaborate with OpenAI team & community how to enable C-suite to make choices…which are underway right now at enterprises.

projects.title: Show HN: Fermi Poker, a combination of poker betting mechanics with estimation

If you don't want to print out anything, you can also use fermi.org/play to see the questions on your device. Fermi Poker combines the betting mechanics of poker with Fermi estimation questions like "How many new smartphones were sold worldwide in 2024?" or "How many chickens were slaughtered for meat worldwide in 2024?" The aspiration was to create a game that teaches important rationality concepts (Fermi estimation, Bayesian updating, cognitive empathy, world-modeling, emotional regulation, etc.) If you want to host a tournament at your school or university, please consider reaching out as I can provide some funding to cover the cost of poker chips and small prizes.

projects.title: [Dev-circuit-ultra]-自己做的比 OpenSpec 更少上下文、更少流程、更快交付的开发 loop
projects.author: iswalterwu
projects.summary: 这两天优化了自己在用的开发工作流，好处是比 OpenSpec 的上下文维护轻量得多，但不丢框架深度和交付细节。 经过测试，在较短的开发周期下，已经能体现较 OpenSpec 超过 -30% 的 token 成本、-48% 的 cache-read 以及 -51% 的文档维护。仓库里还放了一次单会话的开放任务 A/B，方向和这个一致（模型成本 −29.9%、输入+输出 tokens −36.2%、cache-read −48.6%、留存文档 −51.6%）。 同时，记账与开发完全分离，确保开发过程不会被过期设计或旧想法污染。 [项目地址]( https://github.com/iswalterwu/dev-circuit-ultra) [项目概览]( https://github.com/iswalterwu/dev-circuit-ultra/blob/main/assets/after-setup-en.svg) ## 它是什么 一套面向独立开发者的五步功能开发循环，以 skill 的形式加载到 Claude Code、Codex、pi、DeepSeek Harness 等编码 agent 里： 1. 设计澄清 + 意图卡 2. 单个能独立验收的端到端切片 3. 实现 + 验证 4. 独立审核（普通功能一次；框架级改动加一次结构审） 5. 验收 + 合并 和常见的规格驱动工具不同，它不维护 proposal / tasks / archive，仓库里只保留**现行设计**：设计变了就原地覆盖或删除，功能收尾就删卡。决策历史（包括被否掉的方案）写进项目之外的私有 git 账本；强隔离下，dev 容器没有账本挂载、没有路径、没有凭证，开发 agent 读不到。 这条边界是文件系统级的，不是 prompt 约定。README 里把隔离分成弱 / 中 / 强三档，明确写了只有容器方案才叫"保证"。 ## 最新 A/B：省在哪 同一个 records CLI 开放任务、每个 skill 一个会话、最终交付物盲评： | 相对 OpenSpec | Dev-circuit-ultra | OpenSpec | 差异 | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 模型成本 | $0.0743 | $0.1060 | −29.9% | | 输入 + 输出 tokens | 72,308 | 113,337 | −36.2% | | 缓存读取 tokens | 1,891,968 | 3,678,333 | −48.6% | | assistant 轮次 | 39 | 50 | −22% | | 留存文档 | 2 文件 / 132 行 | 3 文件 / 273 行 | −51.6% | | 盲评总分（30） | 27 | 26 | +1 | 欢迎大家一起探讨，跟大家学习！

projects.title: Show HN: Coldframe, a honeypot that poses as a supermarket fridge controller
projects.author: hedgerow-dev

github.name: hedgerow-dev/coldframe
github.description: Low-interaction honeypot for supermarket refrigeration controllers (Danfoss AK-SM 800A, Dixell XWEB 500)

projects.summary: I built Coldframe, a honeypot that pretends to be a supermarket refrigeration controller. Inspired by the events on industrial fridge installations in the past weeks, I wanted to see what people would try against a convincing fake. To learn more about this I built a honeypot that resembled perfectly the Danfoss AK-SM 800A and Dixell XWEB interfaces. Both of them are recognized on Shodan as real ones (an not as honeypots). It’s one Python file using only the standard library, and it builds on eppser/danfoss-ak-sm-decoy and public research by Synacktiv, Claroty and Ironhackers. Things that were fun to get right: - Matching real units. I used Shodan records of real devices to match header order, page titles, certificate fields and TLS versions. The Danfoss persona sends nginx headers in the same order as a real AK-SM 800A. The Dixell persona sends no Server header and pads its page to exactly 8,202 bytes. - Recognising exploit attempts. It recognises CVE-2025-41450, the Danfoss “code of the day” login bypass, and records whether the submitted code is correct for today. It also tags attempts targeting three other Danfoss CVEs and the XWEB vulnerabilities. - Letting them in. Default logins open a fake store dashboard with defrost buttons, so you see the second move, not just the first. Nothing behind it is real. Two instances have been live for a day. So far they’ve only seen generic scanners and Shodan’s crawler, which is called refrigerator.census.shodan.io. Feedback welcome, especially from anyone who has seen these devices in the field!

projects.title: Show HN: A terminal viewer for plain text data files (JSON,YAML,CSV,XML,)
projects.author: rjrodger
projects.summary: When I started working hands-on with OpenAPI specifications, it became clear very quickly that using an editor to read large volumes of deeply nested JSON sucks, a very great deal. So I went looking for something to help, and came across https://jless.io This is an awesome terminal app for navigating nasty JSON documents. I am forever indebted to Paul Martinez for writing this tool. But it did have some gaps. It couldn't reload files that had changed, keeping your place in the JSON structure, which I really needed. And it only loaded one file at a time. But unfortunately it was written in Rust, and I didn't know Rust, and back in the pre-AI days that was kind of a huge blocker. But of course once we got models that could actually write decent code, the obvious idea came to me - I'll just add my features and submit a PR! Happy days. Except by that stage my requirements had grown - I also needed to handle many other file formats, like CSV, TOML, INI, and even XML. So I got side-tracked extending another side-project - an easy going JSON parser that supported comments, and trailing commas, the usual sort of thing. During COVID, with a SaaS startup in the events space now on the rocks, I was looking for some distraction and decided to refactor this little easy-going JSON parser of mine. It used a generated parser and was slow. I read some blog posts about how all production-grade language parsers are pretty much hand-crafted recursive descent, and thought, how hard could it be! Five years later, after many many fun experiments, and production use, I ended up with a runtime parser system: https://tabnas.dev This is a quirky approach to parsing that is partly recursive descent, partly a state machine, and mostly empirical hacking. It works, and it's pretty fast, and I use it for real projects. It has the nice property that grammars are dynamic - you don't generate code, the grammar is executed. A fancy regular expression engine, but revved up to parse anything into a proper abstract syntax tree. Now with that in hand, I could return to the original project and create my own version of jless that solved the itches I needed to scratch: a watch mode; multiple tabs; load any data format into a tree structure Now I still don't know Rust. I mean I like the idea, but there are only so many hours in the day. But now we have AI, so now I do get to go to the candy store. Combining jless.io, and tabnas.dev, and my requirements, I built (caused to be built?), aless - the less for any format! Now this is also a nice stress test for the tabnas parsing engine, and I was very pleased about that too. So if you need to review lots of data structure files on the command line, and need a terminal app to do so, this is for you. I can't help but be struck by the irony however that the need for such a thing is much less now - I mostly get agents to look at large JSON documents now. Still, our puny human brains need help sometimes, and this lets me review documents when I need to. It is also really nice and satisfying to see how easy it is to now bring together open source components to create what is essentially personal software. But I think the key thing out of this little project is that the basic physics of software development remain the same. Software should be built from components glued together. Components should have well-defined interfaces. Aim to reduce cognitive load - this is useful to both humans and machines. Yes, the entire thing could be built from scratch, using a textual specification, and be a mire of over-engineered AI slop, and still be perfectly usable. But the way I actually built it, with AI as a coding companion, using components was deeply satisfying because I still understand the essence of the code, while being able to ignore the accidental complexity. Components give you another layer of abstraction with fewer things to think about, and that allows your human mind to stay in the game.

projects.title: Show HN: GitHub-like reply with "R" for Basecamp and Slack
projects.author: nashbridges
projects.summary: Hello HN! I wrote a browser extension (also available as a userscript) that allows to insert quotes into site's reply message box using selected text + hitting 'r' (as it's done on Github). It targets only specific sites (basecamp.com, slack.com), because that's what we use at our company daily. The idea came out of my boss (who's also a good friend of mine) frustration. He always complained that Basecamp's replies are so inconvenient compared to Github's way. You have to select the quote, copy it into clipboard, then scroll to the reply box, paste it, then select the text again, and finally format it as a quote using editor's toolbar. That's 6 steps vs 2 on Github! Last summer Basecamp rolled out a new facelift featuring a heavy usage of keyboard shortcuts. But "reply with r" was still missing, so another rant from my boss followed :) At that time I was toying with an old browser extension written long time ago as a learning project. I was rewriting it against the new extension API to see what changed/improved. Being immersed into the topic, it was obvious that a thought about "fixing" Basecamp with a browser extension came into my head. So I started working on the Dial R for Reply project during my spare time. I had two clear motivations: 1. I knew it would make someone's life better (myself included). 2. I would learn something new along the way. During the process I realised I could also "fix" Slack replies. It was a bit of trial and error (I didn't use any LLMs for reasons stated above). The hardest part was to dig into each editor's public and private APIs (Basecamp uses lexical, Slack uses Quill). I had to resort to using internals, so be warned -- it might break when site owners decided to update those libraries. On the other hand, hacking a site with an extension is a risky operation anyway (anything may be changed at any time). Key takeaways: 1. browser extensions are cool! Compared to native apps and electron wrappers, you as a customer have such a powerful tool to amend a web application as you like. 2. if you are a library writer, if possible, keep your private state and/or functions accessible to the outside world. Yes, you should clearly mark them as a private, so there's a clear boundary drawn between what can be used safely and what's not. But being able to peek into private state was the only option for me to debug and hack into the application.

projects.title: Show HN: Aggregate Finance, your financial data in a spreadsheet you own
projects.author: mitchthebaker
projects.summary: I started building Aggregate Finance a couple of years ago because I was manually updating a Google Sheet to track my credit card statements, monthly recurring transactions, and spending habits. This seemed perfect for automation as I was having to log in to six separate banking apps to pull this information together. My original intention was to use this tool locally, but I figured it would be an excellent learning opportunity to understand how to scale the application for others to use. The core functionality of Aggregate Finance revolves around syncing banks and brokerages through Plaid to create visuals and data analytics in Google Sheets and OneDrive/Excel, but I've also added Stripe for payments, passkey and TOTP support for MFA (wanted to better learn how WebAuthn works, mostly), and Resend for emailing account updates. The first question you're likely thinking is: isn't this just reinventing the wheel? There's plenty of other personal finance/budgeting apps out there like Rocket Money, Monarch, Copilot Money, YNAB, Tiller, Credit Karma, etc. I personally tried Rocket Money but it left a bad taste in my mouth how my entire financial history was stored on their servers without having direct ownership of the data. Another pain point with these personal finance apps is you're locked into their subscription and lose access to your financial data if you cancel. That's why I opted for the Google Sheet and OneDrive/Excel approach since this persists financial data over time and provides direct data ownership. There's a fair argument that these options still share your financial data with Google or Microsoft, so I built a way to download your financial data locally via CSV/Excel/LibreOffice exports. In terms of data encryption, Aggregate Finance encrypts financial data before it reaches MongoDB: balances, transactions, merchants, statements, holdings, and any user customizations. Each user gets their own AES-256 key rather than a shared key. The reason I went with this approach is for data deletion: when someone deletes their account, their encryption key is deleted as well, so any financial data stored in prior database backups can't be decrypted. I've been using Aggregate Finance with my own live bank accounts and investment holdings, and it's already been helpful. I can see when my credit card statements are due, monitor my entire investment portfolio, keep track of recurring charges, create budgets, and see how my spending pans out over a given month or over the past year. I'm curious whether it's useful for anyone else, and I'd of course welcome any feedback on how I can improve it. You can try it with a free sample spreadsheet that contains a year of example data with no bank connection required at https://app.aggregatefi.com .

projects.title: Show HN: Ferry, a highly customizable and feature-rich file manager for macOS
projects.author: jailbirdBD
projects.summary: I am the main developer of Ferry. The team I am part of began on the demoscene in the mid-90s, but for a long while we are mainly just an indie development studio. Ferry started with me being forced to use macOS at my current workplace, which suddenly replaced a working environment I'd been using during professional career as a programmer: Windows for around 10 years, then Debian/KDE for the last 15 years. Over that time, I'd grown very accustomed to Total Commander on Windows, and later Dolphin on Linux as a file manager, plus a collection of small but very useful tools I'd written for myself on Linux. Moving to macOS was quite an adjustment. I really struggled with Finder and the rather fragmented ecosystem of apps, especially when I couldn't find tools that covered the things I was used to having at my fingertips. Having already written a few internal tools in Swift at work, I started to get familiar with the language while trying out several file managers for macOS without finding one that really suited all of my needs... So one thing led to another, and I eventually decided to build my own version of a better Finder (that's probably how most of the macOS file managers started their journey). Obviously, the first versions were essentially a combination of a slightly improved dual-pane Finder spiced up with basic features from TC, but t'was more than good enough for me. Once I started sharing it with coworkers and friends they began suggesting features I hadn't even considered initially, many of which turned out to be genuinely useful. I know there are quite a lot of file managers out there, so a "what makes Ferry different?" is a totally valid question. Well, Ferry first and foremost tries to be as less opinionated and as much customizable as it's possible, so I have included A LOT of options for personalization. Eg. the layout, the UI, the menus, or the shortcuts are adjustable in many ways, you could even put together something which more or less resembles an old-school Norton Commander-style file manager with a modern toolset if that's your thing. The app also includes a rather big collection of handy tools and tidbits which probably don't seem too interesting up until the point you run into a specific trivial task, and then you realize you have to search and install a tool for it. Main features list: https://ferry.indus3.org/#ftrs Another aspect that's important to me is how the app is made. Having been really involved in the demoscene, I wanted to handcraft as much code as possible and keep AI involvement to a minimum, while still using it to improve quality. Most of Ferry is still written manually, AI mainly helps with the boring parts: proofreading and translations, debugging, tests, temporary tools, code reviews and the site. LLMs have become so advanced that I'm honestly not sure whether this is a good or bad thing for software quality. My skills probably aren't quite on par with a modern LLM agent, but hopefully I can still build something useful and pragmatic by doing most of the work myself. Licensing follows TC's approach: there's a reminder, but you can keep using the app for as long as you like (or until the reminder gets too annoying). Hopefully that's reasonable enough. But if I eventually become really happy with the codebase, I'll most likely release the source code too. At this point, since there are plenty of features, I'm becoming much less interested in adding even more of them and rather focused on getting the existing ones as good as possible: size, stability, performance, memory consumption and above all, bugfixes and code quality. Of course I still listen to users, and if someone suggests a feature which is practical and it improves the UX, I try to include it into a future release. Feel free to contact us, as suggestion and criticism is always welcome!

github.description: An agent paradigm built on an event-driven timeline and a fully plugin-based runtime — it grows and iterates within the environment it runs in.

projects.summary: 我们开源了 Dim，一个以事件时间线为核心的 Agent Harness。 我们希望 Agent 不只是响应一轮轮对话，还能回顾历史、并行探索，并持续推进目标。随着模型越来越聪明，Agent 架构也需要改变：少一些约束，多一些引导，让模型有更大的空间去理解、探索和行动。 主要特点 1. 以事件时间线驱动 Agent 许多 Agent Harness 以消息列表和模型请求为中心，Dim 以一条持续延伸的事件时间线为核心。用户输入、Agent 的判断和行动、工具结果，以及 Harness 自身的工作，都是时间线上的事件。事件写入后不可更改并被分发，负责消费和处理事件的状态机叫 capability。所以 Agent 的历史不只有对话，还有它的观察、行动和结果。 2. 结构化召回历史 内置 recall 工具，Agent 可以结构化地召回整条时间线上的过去对话、事件、行动和结果。用户也可以用 /timeline 跳到任意一条历史消息，再编辑、引用、开分支或 Fork。 3. 通过时间线分支“分神” Dim 支持创建时间线分支（branch 工具），让同一个 Agent 在不同分支里并行探索、反思和推进多条任务线。分支与主分支共享同样的资源和规则。这和 subagent、多 Session 协作不同，是同一个“我”在不同分支里思考和工作。/goal 就是基于分支的目标推进模式。 4. 用插件构造 Agent 的躯体 Dim 基于 rutis 构建多插件体系，会话、模型、工具、权限、审批等能力都是按所有者划分的部件。插件目前可以用 Rust、TypeScript 或 Python 编写。同时支持 MCP、Skills，提供 ACP stdio 网关，也内置 Web 工作区（/web）。 体验 alpha 版 目前提供 alpha 体验版，是单独的 npm 包，命令是 dima： sh npm i -g dimcode-alpha@alpha dima --version dima 支持 macOS / Linux / Windows 的 arm64 和 x64。 首次使用：用 /connect 配置第三方模型的 API Key；如果有 Dim 官方订阅，也可以用 /login 登录使用。 数据放在独立的 ~/.dimcode-alpha，不读写 ~/.dimcode。 默认需要审批工具调用，沙箱为可选开启。 这是预发布版本，接口和行为可能变化。 一起把它做好 Dim 以 MIT 协议开源，欢迎基于它实践自己的想法。上手遇到问题、说明不清楚，或者有想探索的场景，欢迎到仓库 Issues 留下具体反馈。架构文档和 ADR 都在仓库的 docs/ 里，想研究 Agent 运行时设计的可以直接读。

projects.title: Show HN: Penthera, offline pentest security scanner (open-source, rule-based)
projects.author: danosz
projects.summary: local non-AI security for your app/site! For years I had a long .txt file with hundreds of manual security checks I ran before pushing a (client) app/site to live; I am really a rookie compared to the real cyber experts, but just covering the basics has saved us many times from malicious attacks on our infrastructure. With the sprawl of AI generated vibecoded apps (I love it, i think creating should be accessible, but so should be cyber safety) and AI coding tools, our code goes to LLM providers but we'd never know what exactly happens behind the scene, hype harness is just rules imo. As i've started my phd and not building apps (anymore for a living;) I'd decided to open source my rule-based system with some easy onboarding; use it through CLI, NPM, MCP, skill/agent (whatever they might call it in a few years). Its super helpful as a free, open-source alternative to run these checks in your codebase. Having a non-AI solution that costs $0 tokens might not outperform a SOTA security model of a big company; but running internal blue/red hat pentests 24/7/365 should be the norm for a safer internet; having it open-source making it a whitebox system and I hope many people contribute their lists. Its not bulletproof but we score #1 on some public benchmarks among free tools (npm malware, PyPI malware and JS injection bugs) so thats encouraging you can run it pre-commit hook, CI etc - working on a "watch" function that runs it live. Have some flags like --deep for a very intense pentest (SQLi, SSTI, SSRF, XSS, command injection) so be careful and only your own URLs. Also --ai opts-in a local Ollama (or if you want paid also fine) model to find things beyond my rules (the LLM never decides on findings). After you can pass it to you coding agent to fix it; thats up to you. maybe in future ill improve this UX but like to stay local-offline-first anyway feel free to try and give feedback or do a PR if you have some ideas. no signup, $0, local, hackable; read more on the www: penthera.org for some research i've done to make it better/transparent npx penthera --repo . <3 daan

But copying them over, looking them up in a dictionary and making my own flashcards? I was too lazy. So I built a full dictionary into the app, with native speaker pronunciation and verified example sentences from PONS and wiktionary, so you can save a word the moment you don't understand it, or when you're missing one in a conversation. That let me practise situations like sending a package at the post office beforehand. Butt to be honest, it worked in some situations, and in others I failed completely. People speak too fast, use different words, and you can't practise every situation. I really needed to train my general listening comprehension, and YouTube seemed like the best place for that. So I added a YouTube integration: you watch videos, get a comprehension question from time to time, and can add any word to your vocabulary with one click. It's free, with no ads and no premium tier. You can check it out here: https://noentiendo.app I'm happy about any feedback and ideas. Maybe you're learning a language right now and think "it would be cool to practise it that way". Let me know! I've already added German, so if you want a specific language supported, just comment.

projects.title: Show HN: A decent text-to-image model trained for ~$20K (Apache 2.0 Weights)
projects.author: schopra909
projects.summary: My brother and I run a 2-person lab that trains our own generative video models from scratch. The ultimate goal is a set of creative tools that make it easier for anyone to make animation. Video models today are too slow/expensive and lack sufficient controls. Creativity is an iterative process. You make, you tweak, you get better. In our opinion, they're not usable yet for storytelling. When we set out to build Linum v3 (our next video model) earlier this year, the primary goal was to bring the cost envelope of inference down significantly. If our model is fast and cheap, it's the first step (of many) towards useful creative tools. Typically, you see "latent diffusion models". A VAE (Variational Autoencoder) compresses the input data into a smaller "latent space" and the diffusion model learns how to generate within this subspace. Over the past few months, we've been publishing our work on efficient pixel-space diffusion models. These throw away the VAE, having the diffusion model learn a latent-space optimized for its exact task. This serves 3 purposes: 1) Simplify Architecture (no 2-stage model training) 2) Faster Convergence (11x faster convergence vs. our latent diffusion counterpart) 3) Cheaper Inference (4x more aggressive token reduction in attention context-windows, without significant loss in quality) This past month we were pressure testing our latest architecture (Pyramid-JiT) by training a text-to-image model longer than the typical one-off experiment. Specifically, we trained it for ~$20K on 660M samples. We were surprised by the quality of results, so we thought we'd release it as open weights for the community (Apache 2.0). The research itself is already public, on our website. For us, it's a big stepping stone towards cheaper video models, since pretty much all video models start as image models. We like to say these models have to learn nouns before they learn verbs.

projects.title: Show HN: Cppbolt – A lightweight C++ to WebAssembly compiler written in Rust
projects.author: ajtimepyro
projects.summary: Hey HN! I've been working on cppbolt, a lightweight C++ to WebAssembly compiler written in Rust. The idea was to build something that can compile and run C++ directly in the browser without downloading a massive LLVM/Clang toolchain. Unlike projects that bundle LLVM/Clang and can require 100+ MB of compiler assets, cppbolt's compiler payload is around 1 MB. It compiles a supported subset of C++17 directly to standard WebAssembly binaries. Some things it supports: - Classes, inheritance, virtual functions and operator overloading - Templates and a subset of the C++ standard library - Pointers, references, arrays and dynamic memory - Lambdas, structured bindings and range-based loops It comes with a browser playground, CLI and npm package. A few caveats: this is still a work in progress, it doesn't implement the full C++17 standard, and it might not work as expected with certain C++ programs. I'm particularly interested in feedback on the compiler architecture, language support and potential use cases and also interested in connecting with someone who might want to use it in their application. Try it out: - Playground: https://ajtimepyro.is-a.dev/cppbolt/ - Docs: https://ajtimepyro.is-a.dev/cppbolt/book/ - GitHub: https://github.com/AJTimePyro/cppbolt - npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/cppbolt Would love to hear what you think, especially from people who've worked on compilers or WebAssembly.

projects.author: Labo333
projects.summary: Hi HN! I made this fun app which combines quite a few ideas, I thought you might like the story: A few months ago I had the idea of looking for anagrams of names. I started with french names using official statistics about first and last names, which also gave me a pretty simple model for likely anagrams: P(first + last) = P(first) * P(last). Then, I started checking which anagra-names (I coined the term) appeared in the 2021 Facebook leak. Finally, I improved my ranking using a factorization model. All this is available as a light and fast webpage thanks to a lot of cool algorithmic tricks detailed here: https://louisabraham.github.io/anagranames/how.html About the use of AI: Claude Code was fantastic for building the frontend (including the interactive globe) and writing the MLX code (I would otherwise have used PyTorch, which is slower on my machine). It also handled the quantization with very little guidance, which was particularly useful since I'm not an expert in that area. That said, I'm glad I learned CS before LLMs existed and still master it enough to work out the ideas and specs for everything else in my head / on paper before handing the implementation over to the agent.

projects.author: my6666
projects.summary: 陪孩子学习时做起来的交互演示网站，最近做了恐龙专题，一共 64 个演示，打开浏览器就能玩，看不用登录。网站： https://gewujian.cn - 恐龙与远古爬行动物（ 52 种）： https://gewujian.cn/topics/3rtJmOpiescIKQd4qoH24A - 关于恐龙的十二个问题： https://gewujian.cn/topics/dSg0HucUqW5yOr_r_rjh2A ![恐龙与远古爬行动物专题目录]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/SHrWzciHwybsKvQScZ0Udw.png) 孩子看恐龙书，常问「它真的长这样吗？」「颜色是怎么知道的？」。所以这组演示最在意的一件事，是把**知道的**和**猜的**分开：每条关于身体、行为、颜色的说法前面都有小标记，标明是化石看到的、有证据的推测，还是想象；还有争议的，把几种说法并排讲；每条后面的小数字点开就是出处。 几个我自己比较喜欢的： **[霸王龙]( https://gewujian.cn/view/AMol1qNGeB0N14qG68GgOA)** ：三维复原，拖动转着看、滚轮放大，可以让它张嘴，还能切换「有嘴唇 / 没嘴唇」两种复原，这件事到现在还有争议。拖滑杆让身体变透明，能看到里面的骨架。体长、体重按 Sue 这具骨架来比，顺便比一比它有几头大象重。 ![霸王龙]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/lhoc2L5H0lbCREzcFLD7sw.png) **[霸王龙见过剑龙吗？]( https://gewujian.cn/view/R-K6p6c32-Qmag-NRQBWAQ)** ：一面岩壁，越往下越老，一站一站往下挖。挑两只恐龙，先猜「能见面」还是「见不到」，再看两段年代叠不叠、是不是同一套岩层：霸王龙和三角龙能见面；剑龙就不行，它和霸王龙相隔的时间比霸王龙到今天还长。 ![霸王龙和三角龙能见面吗]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/Cs_fh-_n_3BPsVaJq9PoGQ.png) **[鸟真的是恐龙吗？]( https://gewujian.cn/view/0Zkyr7u_gcFuUJOfnz_FVQ)** ：一棵从 2.3 亿年前长到今天的演化树，沿着通向鸟的那一枝往上走，看羽毛、叉骨、翅膀是一样一样先后出现的，不是一下子出现的。 ![恐龙怎样变成鸟]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/PXUVlLeIzMINESaS67DB7A.png) ![三角龙]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/Bk61jQnxwSoBFQSaNY-oLQ.png) 其他还有[三角龙]( https://gewujian.cn/view/uBcGglrHgawFyOEeBzH2ZA)、剑龙、腕龙、始祖鸟等 52 个物种页，禄丰龙、马门溪龙、华阳龙、青岛龙、永川龙、羽王龙这些中国的恐龙也都在。翼龙、蛇颈龙、鱼龙、沧龙、异齿龙名字里带「龙」，但都不是恐龙，单独放在一组讲为什么不是。问题页还有恐龙吃什么、怎样走路和奔跑、角和骨板有什么用、为什么灭绝等。 一些做法： - 每个物种页都有地质时间轴（拖一拖看它生活在多少年前、同时期还有谁）和化石产地地图。 - 页面上有「可以问孩子」的小问题，适合陪孩子边玩边聊。 - 都支持中英文切换，切换时画面状态不会重置。 - 电脑和平板体验最好，手机能看但不如大屏。

AI or machine learning appeared in 50% of 2026 posts, up from 17% in 2019. 2. Most employers posted in only one month. Across all 94 monthly threads, 53% of the employers we identified appeared in just one month. 3. Frontend roles fell from 16% to 3% of posts. That’s a substantial shift in the kinds of developers companies explicitly say they’re looking for. 4. Staff-level posts grew 3.6×. Posts naming staff-level roles rose from 77 in 2019 to 277 in 2026, even as the hiring board got smaller. 5. Only 41 posts explicitly named junior roles in 2026. Out of 2,932 posts. In 2019, there were 163. ... plus 20 other trends. It feels like there's plenty to consider and discuss. Hope it's useful.

I've been working on Rivermark for a few months now to tackle this issue. It's an infinite canvas with an agent that excels at creating on-brand visual content for socials, marketing, and to some extent print. The agent is extremely context-aware and fast (we call it a "short horizon" agent). It will ingest anything and run with it - from Google Sheets copy/paste to .zip files with brandkits or photo sets. Everything is editable manually like in Figma too. We found it works best for people who are not designers but who know what looks good. MCP features to connect it to your agents are coming soon. We're powered by superfast inference at almost 1000 tokens per second and a custom realtime harness, meaning the agent is non-blocking and always responsive, and even has a non-turn-based voice mode that you can just talk into. projects.title: Show HN: An ant simulation whose search walk is tested against real ant tracks
projects.author: hokapo
projects.summary: I've been building an ant simulation that runs in the browser, and thought maybe someone would have fun playing around with it for a few minutes. I always stop and look at ant colonies when I go past them in nature, and thought it would be fun to try to simulate them. I was inspired by Sebastian Lague's and Pezzza's Work's ant videos. I first made this quite advanced simulation with food, predators, competing colonies, queens making new colonies, and hunger. But then I started thinking how realistic it is, and it sent me down a rabbit hole, finding research papers on the topic, and making a model of how real ants walk in real-life experiments. The "realistic" walk is on by default, and you can turn it off to see how it compares to a random walk. The research paper I got the real ant data from showed that the ants' walks aren't a simple random walk, by comparing the times they cross their own path to that of a random walk, and I took their ideas and metrics further when making my own model. It's not perfect, but I'd say it's good enough for now. For now I focused only on the walking patterns when the ants are searching for food, and not on how they follow pheromone trails or how they find their way home. Those are educated guesses in the simulation, but maybe I'll try to replicate real ant behaviour on those too later. If you're interested in the process, and how my model differs from a random walk, and where it falls short, I made a YouTube video out of it. It includes a quiz where you try to spot which paths are by real ants and which are by my model. I'd be interested to see how well the model does in that test. Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zz6LKJT3qow
