projects.title: Show HN: Thinker – Trim context and cache knowledge to extend agent usage limits
projects.author: yoavshmariahu
projects.summary: I’ve been doing a lot of solo development lately and found myself hitting Claude token limits halfway through the week constantly. Even with a Max plan, I’d have to switch over to Codex or Cursor, and it would be a bit difficult to get used to the nuances of each harness. It’s still a problem for me, but I finally built Thinker to save me some tokens and help me get a bit more out of my coding agent subscriptions. I started off a bit in the dark about how token billing works, and had to dig deeper to figure out what workflows ended up hurting my budget the most. By far, it was large context windows. Claude tries to help out on costs by offering prompt caching - which is sort of a bandage on the bigger problem: context bloat. I find that my context window gets bloated with unneeded tokens in two main ways: Tool outputs from subtasks that are long finished. File reads, Bash commands, MCP outputs, etc. Main idea is that the model finished the work but carries the weight of it for every subsequent call - translating to wasted token usage. CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md getting way too big. Lots of content gets dumped into these files as your agents work in your repo. I found that it’s not clear what is actually useful to be included there. Every token here counts, because it will be paid for in every session, and its cost scales linearly with the duration of your session. Thinker addresses both of these issues. We have a proxy that wires in between your harness and model to cut out old context that we determine is no longer needed for your current task. Based on the provider you’re using, we determine the right time to batch enough context to cut that justifies the cache re-write cost, which gets paid off after X subsequent calls. We also analyze your sessions and figure out which parts of your instruction files don’t really get used - and send you suggestions to cut or compress those sections. Thinker will kick off a subagent to do that work for you and open a PR you can review. Finally, we use your sessions to record knowledge notes by distilling your sessions with a cheap model (Haiku, Luna). These notes are then served at prompt time via a cross-encoder, also on your machine, that decides whether a note is relevant to the user’s prompt. Here are some data points to show how exactly Thinker saves you coding agent costs: https://thinker.sh/see-the-data If you’re hitting problems at all with usage limits, it’d be great to hear how you’ve been trying to mitigate it. projects.author: jbspeakr

github.name: zalando-incubator/agentic-identity-broker
github.description: Identity broker for AI agents with OAuth2 delegation and consent management

projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Jan. I am co-author of the Agentic Identity Broker (AIB), an MIT-licensed OAuth2 broker in the Zalando Incubator, that lets a user give an AI agent scoped, revocable access to MCP services. The broker solves three major challenges that are especially relevant in corporate environments: (A) Enable users to delegate workloads to agents without providing the agents all the user’s tokens. (B) Connect fragmented identity and authorization systems. (C) Centralize tool approvals and audit logging. We built AIB to fill an infrastructure gap in our own agent platform. At this moment in time, IETF working groups are still finalizing standards for agent identity, and vendors are still turning the necessary infrastructure into off-the-shelf products. We needed that infrastructure today. How it works: the user consents once per agent and service. The broker stores the third-party tokens encrypted. At request time a gateway (e.g. Agentgateway) does RFC 8693 token exchange. Agents never see user tokens and MCP servers only implement tools and don’t need to care about all the OAuth 2.1 plumbing. AIB is v0.1 and runs in production, bringing together hundreds of our agents with dozens of internal and external MCP servers. To try it locally: clone the repo, run "just compose-up-detached". The current features focus on on-behalf-of (OBO) use cases, where human actors delegate to agents. Next we are looking to also support headless agents, where agents are invoked by machines. Intent-based authorization is yet another package on our roadmap. If you’ve built either, or have feedback on the UI/UX, I’d like to hear from you!

projects.title: 花了 6 年搭了一个去中心化的社交网络作品
projects.author: printfcoder
projects.summary: AI 真的要淘汰传统的程序员角色了。我大概是在 2019 年有这个想法，那个时候对各大厂商的 App 后台数据上报非常不爽，就想未来有没有一种可能，每个人掌握自己的社交关系？而不是被几个大厂拿去当成护城河。 所以这些年就慢慢找时间往这个方向靠，期间探索、架构、实现都搞过一些玩具版本。进展非常慢，一方面确实是时间不够；另一方面是需要相大量的技术储备，前后端、Mobile App 、架构、网络、设计等，都要自己来一个一个去摸索，尝试找了一些朋友，都对这个场景兴趣不是很大，基本只有极少人对隐私、数据保护有相当的诉求，大部分朋友还是习惯于让大公司掌握、管理自己的数据资源，故而在前期找到志合的朋友比较困难。 但是，我们的这些身外之物，我真的认为个人未来最重要的东西就是数据，而不再只是金钱。 我搞的这套方案，是一个去中心化的社交网络。可以简单看看 Desktop 端的运行效果：三个人，三台各自独立部署的节点，没有中心服务器，消息直接在节点之间联邦送达。下面是三个独立节点第一次联邦跑通时的对话。 我暂时给这个方案起名叫 Peers-Touch ，意为大家可以直接轻碰接触。整体思考是通过一个去中心化（联邦式）网络框架，在上头先长了这个社交产品。每个人跑自己的 Home Station ，可以运行在 NAS 、树莓派、云主机都行；身份、关系、消息全在自己手里（也就是个人 Station 上），Station 之间像邮件一样联邦互连，端到端加密，规划中，我也做了 Agent 、小程序和区块链，都跑在自己的 Station 上，作为智能时代和扩展方向的预留。 下图是大体的产品架构 https://i.imgur.com/HNzSw2V.png 再说怎么做出来的。 这个项目 6 年前开工。前几年是传统写法，一个模块一个模块地做；后面基本是我带着 Trae 完成的——一个人，Go / Rust / TS / Kotlin / Swift 五个栈，80 多万行，从架构到真机验收。不是我突然变猛了，是干法变了：做什么、架构怎么定、人怎么排，AI 给；具体写，AI 也给。 视频在这，2 分 52 秒，从节点部署、联邦互联、端到端加密到 Agent 都过了一遍（播放器可能默认压到 360p ，点右下角齿轮切 1080p ）： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZU6kMt3BQrs 代码在这： https://github.com/peers-labs/peers-touch ，还在成长，欢迎拍砖，欢迎 Star 。 一些目前的设想： https://peers-touch.vercel.app/ 最后说点感想。 我当程序员第 14 个年头了，从传统行业、金融、互联网都干过，现在团队正在转行做 Agent 相关的事，虽然也是趋势所迫，不过我也认为 Agent 本身也是过滤，一方面传统行业的技能、知识等，会慢慢向大模型基建下沉，这是已经能看到的事实，未来这个协作过程会从现在的“领域-Agent-LLM”的路径，直接转成“领域-LLM-Infra”，LLM 平台会进一步泛化现在 Agent 的能力变成口语就能驱动的万物即可 Agent 的样子，讲几句话就能做一个自己的 Agent ，当全部都是 Agent 的时候，约等于没有 Agent ，当然只是我的观点。 未来 Idea 到实现会是个比较廉价的过程，AI 挤压我们传统就业空间的矛盾总会有利的一面，大家都可以大胆去选择探索未来。“因为生命有限的，所以我们的选择，都被赋予了重量”。 程序员转不转型，已经不用讨论了。一个人端到端干完这几年，我反而觉得有三样东西更值钱： 1. 想得出新东西。做什么比怎么做稀缺，这轮 AI 替不了。 2. 学得动。新东西到手，几天之内得能拿它干活。 3. 落得了地。从想法到真机跑通、能交付，结果和锅还是你的。 造的过程，也在体验生命的厚度，哪怕失败了也是能接受的。

projects.title: Show HN: Grid – A Hold'em arena where your AI agent plays your strategy (Beta)
projects.author: taelimoh
projects.summary: Hi HN, my friend's team and I have been building a game called GRID, a dog poker game with an AI twist. Under the cute dog graphics, GRID is an arena where LLMs compete, with no-limit hold’em as the medium. You duke it out as a strategist, vibe coder, and bot maker. Why: models get compared on benchmarks all the time, but rarely as my agent against yours in its truest form. GRID is our attempt at creating that arena, because we believe this type of game will exist in the future, as AI becomes as common a tool as the browser. How it works: * Paste a prompt and an MCP config into Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client. The agent waits for its turn and sends actions back through tool calls. * The strategy is text written in the game, up to 6,000 characters. We thought it’d be cool to have a preset, “Play like Elon”, to show you what you can do. * You can change the strategy any time, and it applies from the next action. You can even ask your AI to change it for you, based on what it learns about its opponents’ strategies from the match history. * Free beta. Play chips only. We just opened up the game today and are gathering data on how to steer this ship next. Rough edges: * MCP can be finicky, especially if you refresh your browser while in a match. If this happens and you can’t get your agent to connect, wait 5 min and retry | log out using the settings button at the top left and log back in. Stability is currently our top priority. * MCP also uses a lot of tokens, more than the game should, because every tool call costs tokens. We plan to overhaul this with a new connection type in a future version so it’s much more efficient. * There’s a built-in local model for folks who don’t want to use their own AI. It plays basic hold’em OK but struggles to follow written strategies. If you want to try it, I’d recommend leaving your strategy blank. Sadly, it plays best with no instructions. * House bots fill empty seats. We made this choice so matches happen even when only a few people are online. Honestly, I’m most curious how you’d write a strategy that holds up against everyone else’s agents. And if MCP setup breaks on you, please tell me. We'll be in the thread as long as possible.

github.description: A Kanban board for Codex power users to manage concurrent chats, tasks, and usage history. 专为 Codex 重度使用者设计，看板模式管理并发对话，组织对话合集

projects.summary: 产品截图 1: 产品截图 2: 插件使用场景一 插件设计之初是为我自己的需求服务，应该很多人和我一样是 Codex 重度用户，而且会同时开很多个会话，经常是这个会话在出方案、另一个会话在 worktree 写代码、其他还开了一堆的会话在排查线上问题，同时要并行处理很多事情。 当然并行处理并不是阻塞点，毕竟是 AI 处理，阻塞点在于每一个对话结束后都要我们一个一个去 check 才行，这就导致经常会忘记 check，或者不想现在就 check，那随着处理的东西越来越多，之前没有立即 check 的对话，很可能会被漏掉，几十几百个会话里面，漏看一两个是常有的事情，我经常是隔了几天发现这个问题还没被处理，然后来 Codex 根据关键字搜对话，这个时候我又得花时间重新回想一遍这个问题的背景。 甚至有时候会出现你隔了很久来 check 的时候，发现 Codex 竟然需要你输入补充信息，这就更难受了。。。 插件使用场景二 上面我们重点聊的是并行处理的问题，我经常还会遇到的一个场景是，开多个对话分模块来处理同一个需求，然后这个模块的所有内容我都会在同一个对话里进行，这样做的目的是啥呢，就是保证不同的模块的上下文都是连贯的，一个对话专注处理一个模块，拥有我关于这个模块的所有输入。如果需求开发的时间跨度比较长，就经常会忘记某个模块。如果没有这个插件的话，我目前的解法是统一重命名 + 置顶。 再举个例子，就是我们日常工作中还存在很多调研性的需求，这类工作不一定要及时处理，只是先调研，可能到后面某一天的时候来会拿出来，到时候要找的话，要么是关键字搜索，要么就是把这些对话先置顶。这类需求一多，管理起来就越来越麻烦 插件使用场景三 我目前的开发流程基本都是写让 Codex 写方案文档/设计稿 -> Goal 模式实现 -> 出验收文档 -> 推送 MR，对我来说要 check 的就 3 个东西： 1. 方案文档 2. 验收文档 3. MR 链接 所以需要不管我在这个对话中聊了多少轮，这三个东西我都能快速的找到，但现在做不到，我经常需要翻上下文来找 插件介绍 以上，便是这个插件要解决的问题。 Codex-Kanban-Plugin：A Kanban board for Codex power users to manage concurrent chats, tasks, and usage history. 专为 Codex 重度使用者设计，看板模式管理并发对话，组织对话合集 GitHub jingchengyin/codex-kanban-plugin 看板 看板按状态分列： 需要你处理 正在运行 未读（对话已完成但还未读） 空闲（对话已完成且已经完成） 执行异常（比如模型失败，排队超时等等） 看板上展示的信息包括： 所属文件夹 使用的分支/worktree 模型和思考强度 计划模式 目标模式 最近一次的用户输入 最近一次 Codex 处理所花费的 token 和时间 自动解析出来的成果（目前包括 MR 链接 + 计划文档 + 飞书文档） 所属合集 支持自定义配置成果解析 URL： 如果存在需要用户输入的会话，看板卡片会直接展示待确认卡片，可直接在插件内操作，无需跳转会话 合集 对应上述场景二，合集支持把多条对话关联起来，统一管理说明、进度、成果和验收清单。 事项有四个状态：待开始、进行中、待验收、已验收，状态由你手动更新。 看板页面也可以快速加入合集： 合集 icon 和颜色支持自定义： 关于安全性 插件只读访问本机 Codex 对话数据，所有数据均保存在 CODEXHOME/kanban/workspace.sqlite。没设置 CODEXHOME 时，默认位置是 ~/.codex/kanban/workspace.sqlite。 快速安装 目前只支持 MacOS，Windows 暂未适配，欢迎 PR 👏 把下面这段话发给 Codex，让它帮你安装： 请帮我安装 Codex-Kanban-Plugin： 从 main 分支添加插件市场，安装 codex-kanban-plugin@codex-kanban-plugin，并检查安装结果。

projects.title: Show HN: KeepPlain – ask your coding agent why a line of code exists
projects.author: kagen
projects.summary: My code is written by agents now. Git blame shows me the commit and my own name, but the reason for the code is in a session I closed weeks ago. KeepPlain saves your agent sessions. It uses git blame to find the session that corresponds to a file, line, or commit. Then it shows the original request and the reasoning behind the change. It also finds commits made by the user after the agent session and links them to the session. I also try to use the mistakes the agent makes over and over to turn them into rules for new sessions. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi and Antigravity. Your sessions are uploaded to my server and are kept private to you. All secrets are redacted on your machine before the upload. I’m sure there will be lots of questions about this. The plugin is MIT licensed and open source. The server is not. Teams can run their own Postgres database to store their data. KeepPlain is free for personal use and teams will pay for it. I am a solo developer and this is early on in development so please let me know where it breaks.

projects.summary: Here is Cerea, a self-hostable, open-source (Apache 2.0) chat+agent frontend for LLMs. It works alone with any OpenAI-compatible inference provider, but it's way better when coupled with the model gateway I'm also developing, Pystino ( https://github.com/paoloviviani/Pystino ). I came to this after struggling to find a hosted chat interface that was truly open source, that I really enjoyed to use, and that was simple enough to be shared and used by family. In particular, I was looking for something that could provide the smooth and integrated user experience of commercial products for the tasks needed by family (e.g., document editing, form filling, notes and knowledge management), but backed by open models hosted wherever I decide. Then it became richer, now supporting: remote coding agents (wrapping Opencode), delegation and coordination between agents, integration between chat/projects and code agents (this one to me is a pain point for Claude, which I use at work), projects, RAG, rich artifacts support, schedules, and more. You can try it yourself, either cloning the full repo and head to Cerea/kit, or just the deploy kit with a script ( https://github.com/paoloviviani/Cerea#quick-start ). It's just a docker compose with a ./configure script that helps to generate a sensible .env for the specific scenario. It works in the browser and as a PWA on mobile. I hope you'll enjoy, feel free to reach out for questions.

projects.summary: 自荐一个自己开发的开源项目：EPUB Reading Edition（MIT）。本人是项目作者。 这是一个供 AI 编程助手使用的 EPUB 阅读与文档处理工具（AI Agent Skill），用于将用户有权处理的 EPUB 整理为带阅读导读的 Word 文档和离线 HTML 阅读器。 主要功能： EPUB 结构解析：依据 OPF manifest、spine、目录和文档结构识别阅读顺序与阅读单元，保存结构化 JSON。 AI 阅读辅助：由助手阅读全文及相关图表，撰写中文「背景」与「作者观点」两段导读。 多格式输出：生成 Word、可直接打开的单文件 HTML，以及静态网站 ZIP。 阅读标记：支持黄色高亮、部分取消和按原文顺序复制高亮；标记保存在当前浏览器本地。 AI Agent 负责阅读理解与导读，Python 负责提取、数据校验和文档/HTML 生成；脚本不内置模型 API，不能仅运行 Python 就自动完成 AI 阅读。 项目最初来自我个人改善 The Economist EPUB 精读体验的需求，之后整理成可复用工作流。目前仍保留部分专用解析规则，已用原创合成 EPUB 验证解析、Word/HTML 导出与高亮功能，不宣称兼容所有 EPUB；具体限制见 README。 仓库仅提供工具代码、模板和原创合成测试素材，不提供原刊文件或下载服务。使用者需确认输入、AI 处理和输出分享的相应权限；持有文件或订阅不自动等于获得这些许可。项目与 The Economist 没有官方合作、授权或隶属关系。

projects.summary: Hi HN, I run Quanterlab which is a quantitative research platform (can as well be described as backtesting tool for trading and investing ideas) and it‘s purpose is to provide interpretable results for users' own rule sets, using point-in-time data. I am coming from mechanical engineering domain and I wanted to reflect the concepts of engineering. For example, the “strategies” or more elaborately put “market inefficiency hypothesis” are constructed as block diagrams. And in its own style, QuanterLab is quite a strange thing for a finance software. Instead of looking at candle sticks, this is to construct a logic with these block diagrams. Each one of the boxes have certain contracts with each other’s and it is all about stopping people to make things that does not make sense. Information leakage is something I care a lot and for that purpose everything constructed is placed automatically on a timeline showing you which piece of the block is using which time window which is intended as a visual safety net. And also, the AI is big part of it, which I am personally happy with my decisions on how it is implemented. AI is allowed to use tools in the platform to construct what you describe and deliver the news to you. So, it is definitely NOT something that AI exploiting information uncontrolled (overfit) and adding creativity with what you did not ask for. Similarly, the platform is available as MCP servers and connectors in many AI platforms, and again these AI models only allowed to use the tools that is exposed to them and they are obliged to present the information with certain cards exposing you the blocks to let you inspect or manually change. Lastly, anything constructed can be set as paper trade and you receive a morning brief after every working day. You can try the lab without an account or you can as well connect it to your AI as connector, 10 runs a day for guests and an account gets 30 days of the Practitioner plan, no card needed. Sorry for my awkward mistakes in the text, especially for native English speakers, this text did not pass through AI. Greetings from Germany, Serhat

projects.title: Show HN: Ferry, a highly customizable and feature-rich file manager for macOS
projects.author: jailbirdBD
projects.summary: I am the main developer of Ferry. The team I am part of began on the demoscene in the mid-90s, but for a long while we are mainly just an indie development studio. Ferry started with me being forced to use macOS at my current workplace, which suddenly replaced a working environment I'd been using during professional career as a programmer: Windows for around 10 years, then Debian/KDE for the last 15 years. Over that time, I'd grown very accustomed to Total Commander on Windows, and later Dolphin on Linux as a file manager, plus a collection of small but very useful tools I'd written for myself on Linux. Moving to macOS was quite an adjustment. I really struggled with Finder and the rather fragmented ecosystem of apps, especially when I couldn't find tools that covered the things I was used to having at my fingertips. Having already written a few internal tools in Swift at work, I started to get familiar with the language while trying out several file managers for macOS without finding one that really suited all of my needs... So one thing led to another, and I eventually decided to build my own version of a better Finder (that's probably how most of the macOS file managers started their journey). Obviously, the first versions were essentially a combination of a slightly improved dual-pane Finder spiced up with basic features from TC, but t'was more than good enough for me. Once I started sharing it with coworkers and friends they began suggesting features I hadn't even considered initially, many of which turned out to be genuinely useful. I know there are quite a lot of file managers out there, so a "what makes Ferry different?" is a totally valid question. Well, Ferry first and foremost tries to be as less opinionated and as much customizable as it's possible, so I have included A LOT of options for personalization. Eg. the layout, the UI, the menus, or the shortcuts are adjustable in many ways, you could even put together something which more or less resembles an old-school Norton Commander-style file manager with a modern toolset if that's your thing. The app also includes a rather big collection of handy tools and tidbits which probably don't seem too interesting up until the point you run into a specific trivial task, and then you realize you have to search and install a tool for it. Main features list: https://ferry.indus3.org/#ftrs Another aspect that's important to me is how the app is made. Having been really involved in the demoscene, I wanted to handcraft as much code as possible and keep AI involvement to a minimum, while still using it to improve quality. Most of Ferry is still written manually, AI mainly helps with the boring parts: proofreading and translations, debugging, tests, temporary tools, code reviews and the site. LLMs have become so advanced that I'm honestly not sure whether this is a good or bad thing for software quality. My skills probably aren't quite on par with a modern LLM agent, but hopefully I can still build something useful and pragmatic by doing most of the work myself. Licensing follows TC's approach: there's a reminder, but you can keep using the app for as long as you like (or until the reminder gets too annoying). Hopefully that's reasonable enough. But if I eventually become really happy with the codebase, I'll most likely release the source code too. At this point, since there are plenty of features, I'm becoming much less interested in adding even more of them and rather focused on getting the existing ones as good as possible: size, stability, performance, memory consumption and above all, bugfixes and code quality. Of course I still listen to users, and if someone suggests a feature which is practical and it improves the UX, I try to include it into a future release. Feel free to contact us, as suggestion and criticism is always welcome!

projects.title: Show HN: teletap – Your remote coding agents ask you when stuck
projects.author: megalomanu
projects.summary: Hi HN! I'm Manuel, CTO of Tandem. Most of our PRs are now written by custom coding agents on remote hosts. But we had a recurring problem: they sometimes lacked product context and consequently guessed too much. This resulted in some PRs coming back a bit off, with some wrong choices. We ended up spending more time fixing the PRs than if we had made them ourselves. So we built teletap, first for ourselves, and now for everyone. How it works: when an agent is stuck on something it can't find itself, it asks a person on the team. It picks the best person to help it, based on a short "when to ask" description each developer specifies, like "pricing owner", or AGENTS.md instructions. The question pops up on that engineer's computer. They answer it, and it goes straight back into the agent's session, which is now unblocked and can continue. If the engineer doesn't know, they just have to say so, and the agent will ask someone else. Many teams use Slack for this. We tried it too. But we didn't find it productive enough. The agent had to keep checking a thread. An idle session never saw the reply. With teletap, the answer is delivered directly into the session, even if it's idle. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes and Pi. Just install it on a device (your computer, a VM, a Docker container, a VPS...), and it finds all the installed agents and plugs into them. We were inspired by Tailscale, which we love. Devices talk peer-to-peer, encrypted end to end, and fall back to our relay only when a direct path is impossible (the relay never sees the content). It's very minimal: you don't have to live in another interface. In case you're wondering, we wrote it in Rust and everything runs over QUIC, on a single UDP socket. The most fun part of the project was the integration with agents, figuring out how to put the answer into a live session. For instance, Claude Code has an internal messaging socket (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET), while the messaging for Codex works through its app-server. For pi, we developed a plugin (how surprising). Short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z224uyyxuYQ Website with install instructions: https://teletap.dev We'd love your feedback, especially from teams that run agents in the cloud.

projects.summary: TermQuay（栈桥）是一款开源桌面远程工作台，使用 Go、Wails 和 React 开发，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。它将 SSH、本地终端、SFTP、配置编辑、Linux 监控与 RDP 集中在同一工作区，适合开发者、个人运维和 Homelab 用户。Windows 版单文件约 32 MB，支持多主机巡检、配置历史与验证、跨主机文件复制及加密备份，连接配置数量无商业限制。采用 Apache-2.0 许可证。 亮点 体积小，功能完整：以 v1.3.0 Windows 版为例，压缩包约 12 MB，解压后是一个约 32 MB 的可执行文件，界面资源内嵌，运行需要系统 WebView2。终端输出按界面消费进度控制，传输并发与队列有界，监控面板隐藏后停止采集。 配置变更有完整操作流程：编辑器支持多编码、JSON/YAML 诊断、冲突合并与加密历史，可配置文件验证、reload 和健康检查命令，保存并验证后再确认重载。 多主机执行与判定：支持多步骤、分批执行和首台完成后人工确认；按退出码、文本、正则或 JSON 字段判断巡检结果，也能选定基线主机，比较多台服务器上的配置文件。 文件操作覆盖多台主机：支持成对浏览、文本对比、目录差异预览及复制。跨主机复制经本机流式中转，不生成本地中间文件。 本机管理，自选备份位置：核心使用无需厂商账号，凭据加密保存，可选主密码与应用锁。支持本地和自选 WebDAV 的加密快照备份，恢复前可预览，或将所选连接作为副本导入。 可供外部 Agent 使用：提供本机 CLI 和配套 Skill。桌面启用访问并解锁后，Agent 可以复用已连接的 SSH 工作区，通过精确工作区 ID 执行命令并获取 JSON 结果，无需重新提供 SSH 密码或私钥。 下载： 我是项目作者，本次为自荐。界面目前以简体中文为主。下面的截图来自 macOS 原生应用的演示模式，使用示例主机与数据。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Dim 以事件时间线为核心、全插件化的 Agent Harness（Rust / MIT）
projects.author: zerob13

github.name: arcships/dim
github.description: An agent paradigm built on an event-driven timeline and a fully plugin-based runtime — it grows and iterates within the environment it runs in.

projects.summary: 我们开源了 Dim，一个以事件时间线为核心的 Agent Harness。 我们希望 Agent 不只是响应一轮轮对话，还能回顾历史、并行探索，并持续推进目标。随着模型越来越聪明，Agent 架构也需要改变：少一些约束，多一些引导，让模型有更大的空间去理解、探索和行动。 主要特点 1. 以事件时间线驱动 Agent 许多 Agent Harness 以消息列表和模型请求为中心，Dim 以一条持续延伸的事件时间线为核心。用户输入、Agent 的判断和行动、工具结果，以及 Harness 自身的工作，都是时间线上的事件。事件写入后不可更改并被分发，负责消费和处理事件的状态机叫 capability。所以 Agent 的历史不只有对话，还有它的观察、行动和结果。 2. 结构化召回历史 内置 recall 工具，Agent 可以结构化地召回整条时间线上的过去对话、事件、行动和结果。用户也可以用 /timeline 跳到任意一条历史消息，再编辑、引用、开分支或 Fork。 3. 通过时间线分支“分神” Dim 支持创建时间线分支（branch 工具），让同一个 Agent 在不同分支里并行探索、反思和推进多条任务线。分支与主分支共享同样的资源和规则。这和 subagent、多 Session 协作不同，是同一个“我”在不同分支里思考和工作。/goal 就是基于分支的目标推进模式。 4. 用插件构造 Agent 的躯体 Dim 基于 rutis 构建多插件体系，会话、模型、工具、权限、审批等能力都是按所有者划分的部件。插件目前可以用 Rust、TypeScript 或 Python 编写。同时支持 MCP、Skills，提供 ACP stdio 网关，也内置 Web 工作区（/web）。 体验 alpha 版 目前提供 alpha 体验版，是单独的 npm 包，命令是 dima： sh npm i -g dimcode-alpha@alpha dima --version dima 支持 macOS / Linux / Windows 的 arm64 和 x64。 首次使用：用 /connect 配置第三方模型的 API Key；如果有 Dim 官方订阅，也可以用 /login 登录使用。 数据放在独立的 ~/.dimcode-alpha，不读写 ~/.dimcode。 默认需要审批工具调用，沙箱为可选开启。 这是预发布版本，接口和行为可能变化。 一起把它做好 Dim 以 MIT 协议开源，欢迎基于它实践自己的想法。上手遇到问题、说明不清楚，或者有想探索的场景，欢迎到仓库 Issues 留下具体反馈。架构文档和 ADR 都在仓库的 docs/ 里，想研究 Agent 运行时设计的可以直接读。

projects.title: Show HN: Penthera, offline pentest security scanner (open-source, rule-based)
projects.author: danosz
projects.summary: local non-AI security for your app/site! For years I had a long .txt file with hundreds of manual security checks I ran before pushing a (client) app/site to live; I am really a rookie compared to the real cyber experts, but just covering the basics has saved us many times from malicious attacks on our infrastructure. With the sprawl of AI generated vibecoded apps (I love it, i think creating should be accessible, but so should be cyber safety) and AI coding tools, our code goes to LLM providers but we'd never know what exactly happens behind the scene, hype harness is just rules imo. As i've started my phd and not building apps (anymore for a living;) I'd decided to open source my rule-based system with some easy onboarding; use it through CLI, NPM, MCP, skill/agent (whatever they might call it in a few years). Its super helpful as a free, open-source alternative to run these checks in your codebase. Having a non-AI solution that costs $0 tokens might not outperform a SOTA security model of a big company; but running internal blue/red hat pentests 24/7/365 should be the norm for a safer internet; having it open-source making it a whitebox system and I hope many people contribute their lists. Its not bulletproof but we score #1 on some public benchmarks among free tools (npm malware, PyPI malware and JS injection bugs) so thats encouraging you can run it pre-commit hook, CI etc - working on a "watch" function that runs it live. Have some flags like --deep for a very intense pentest (SQLi, SSTI, SSRF, XSS, command injection) so be careful and only your own URLs. Also --ai opts-in a local Ollama (or if you want paid also fine) model to find things beyond my rules (the LLM never decides on findings). After you can pass it to you coding agent to fix it; thats up to you. maybe in future ill improve this UX but like to stay local-offline-first anyway feel free to try and give feedback or do a PR if you have some ideas. no signup, $0, local, hackable; read more on the www: penthera.org for some research i've done to make it better/transparent npx penthera --repo . <3 daan

projects.title: Show HN: Nico – a two-agent type personal agent on your Mac
projects.author: benjushi
projects.summary: Hi HN. I'm Brian, I make Xmind, the most popular mind mapping app, since 2006. This is my new project Nico, a personal agent for the Mac. Every huge companies are building personal agents right now. The part I think matters most is the two-agent structure, so that's what Nico is built around. The front agent talks to you. Always available, only one session, one memory, continuously compaction, and it carries almost no tools, so it can answer fast. The worker agent does the job. It picks up tasks the front agent puts in an inbox and reports back when they're done. It almost never talks to you; anything it needs goes through the front agent. I think this is the real step forward, but the attention goes to the cloud computer. I get why: you can hand the agent a task from your phone. But, it also makes everything more complicated. People need to upload the entire environment while So I built one with the cloud computer taken out. Nico is a native Mac app. You hold the right ⌘ key (or fn) and talk; the front agent answers by voice; the worker agent is pi (github.com/earendil-works/pi) runs by your own AI subscription, in a sandbox. With computer-use (via cua-driver), browser-use (via a browser extension), and a built-in browser, she can clean up your desktop, or answer "why is my Mac so hot". If you say "this", she looks at the screenshot of the active window. Most tasks run without you; sending an email waits for your click. The downside: when you're not at your Mac, you can't use it. I haven't figured out what to do about that. Would you want a personal agent that only lives on your Mac?

projects.title: Show HN: I paid Claude US$1,070 to read the worst reviews of 30k places to stay
projects.author: orifito
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Oriol, a solo developer in Barcelona. Before booking anything, I used to do the same thing every time: find a place with a great rating, open the lowest-rated reviews and read them one by one. Broken AC, thin walls, a bed as hard as a board, a shower that barely works. Very often the deal-breaker was right there, written by guest after guest, under a lovely 8.9 global score. OKstays does that reading for you. It scores 33,000+ places to stay in 95 destinations on how well you'll actually sleep and stay there, and ranks them for how you travel (light sleeper, remote work, family...). This month I re-scored 30,500 places from what guests wrote. For each one, Claude reads its newest and lowest-rated reviews, then a second search collects what about 7 other review and booking sites say. It scores 67 comfort signals from 0 to 10, each with a short reason you can read on the place's page. If a deal-breaker (dirty rooms, an uncomfortable bed, a poor shower, bugs) ends up at 6.0 or below, the place is left out of every ranking. One angry guest can't do that alone: it has to be a pattern. What came out (method and charts: https://okstays.com/stats/deal-breakers ): - 1 in 39 places to stay has a deal-breaker guests keep reporting. - Half of them come down to a poor shower (51%). Bugs are next (35%). - 92% of them still have a guest rating of 8+. Across all places, it's 97%. - Under US$100 a night, deal-breakers are nearly 4.5x as common as at US$400+. - Among hotels: about 1 in 5 in New Delhi, 1 in 19 in Mexico City, and 1 of 698 in Tokyo. The cost, because HN always asks: about US$1,070 in API calls, US$3.7 cents a place, all batched (first search ~US$1.3c, second search ~US$1.2c, scoring ~US$1.2c). Before spending it, I tested methods against places I had researched in depth. My old scores were off by about 1.1 points on average; reading reviews brought that to about 0.5 (on a different, larger reference set, so read it as a direction, not a precise gain). It's free, no sign-up, and it also works inside ChatGPT, Claude and Grok as a connector (okstays.com/mcp). It earns booking commissions, and hotels can't pay to rank or to be removed. Last month it earned its first US$8.81, 18 months after I started. That was also the first money I ever made online. Two things I'd love from you: pick a city you know well and tell me if the top 5 feels right. Thank you!

projects.author: Coooolfan

github.name: Coooolfan/XiaomiAlbumSyncer
github.description: 全量/增量/定时 下载 小米云/iCloud 服务中的 相册/录音 到本地

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个我独立开发的开源自托管工具 Xiaomi Album Syncer（GPL-3.0）。 小米云服务一直没有官方的相册批量导出入口，想把自己云端的相册拿回本地，只能手动在桌面客户端选中下载。这个项目就是解决这件事：登录账号后，它把小米云端的相册（录音）完整拉到本地硬盘或 NAS，之后可以定时跑增量同步，已下载过的文件自动跳过。除小米云服务外也支持 Apple iCloud 照片，多个账号可以放在一个实例里统一管理。 主要功能： 全量 / 增量：用 Cron 表达式设定时，增量只拉新增资产，跑一遍大相册也只要几秒 自动维护凭据：小米支持手机扫码登录，iCloud 走账号密码 + 2FA，凭据过期自动刷新或者通知 照片时间线：下载时回填照片视频的 Exif 拍摄时间和文件系统修改时间，导入 Immich 等本地相册后按拍摄日期归档 按相册归档：每个云端相册存成独立目录，下载路径支持表达式插值自定义（比如按账号/相册/年月） Web UI 与 MCP Server：扫码、建任务、看下载记录都在浏览器里完成（支持 Passkey 和 HTTPS）；也可以把实例挂给 AI 助手，用自然语言查进度、触发任务 部署是典型自托管方案：Docker 一键拉起，或者直接下载单文件可执行程序，Linux / macOS / Windows 全平台含 arm64，面向 NAS 常驻。后端 Kotlin + Solon，前端 Vue 3。 bash docker run -d \ p 8232:8080 \ v ~/xiaomi-album-syncer/download:/app/download \ v ~/xiaomi-album-syncer/db:/app/db \ coolfan1024/xiaomi-album-syncer:latest

projects.title: Living Brain
projects.summary: Every AI conversation contains knowledge worth keeping, but most of it gets trapped in separate chats and tools. projects.title: Show HN: Firenook – Firebase emulators in Rust: 40× faster writes, 10× less RAM
projects.author: sanjevirau
projects.summary: Hi HN. I build with Firebase almost every day and keep the local emulators running all day, and two things wore me down. The suite is really heavy. Java is required, a heap that grew past 22 GiB on our app, out-of-memory crashes, and data gone at every stop unless you export it. It had become almost unusable and was slowing us down. It's also hard to see what your app is doing. The Emulator UI is incomplete, with no page for Functions, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks or Eventarc, only a log. Firenook replaces the emulators for Firestore, Auth, Storage, Functions, Extensions, and many other services with native Rust services. It's a drop-in replacement, so simply install one npm package, no Java, change `firebase emulators:start` to `firenook emulators:start`, and your firebase.json, ports, SDKs, rules and Functions code stay as they are. We tested it heavily. On two hours of a real app's traffic, Firenook peaked at 2.11 GiB against 22.57 GiB on official emulator and answered writes in 5.1 ms against 208 ms at the median. On an idle emulator a write is only 1.5× faster and 40× is under load. With --keep-data, millions of documents come back in about 0.5s. Results are here: https://firenook.dev/benchmarks The console sits on the Emulator UI's port. It shows every function call with its logs and stack, and you can run a failed one again. It shows your rules beside each decision, with the line that decided it, and an inbox of the emails and codes Auth would have sent. Screenshots: https://firenook.dev/console . Honestly, I built the console from scratch as the one the emulators should have had from the start. It's fast, clean, full of the detail you need while developing, and still able to browse and edit millions of documents. The terminal shows a start-up card, then one line per function call with its outcome and, when it fails, the stack. And `npx firenook mcp add` gives Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code tools over the running emulators, so an agent can read the logs or ask the rules why a request was denied, without touching production. It's still new and I'm sure it misses things, so if you use the Firebase emulators, I'd love for you to try it on your project. `npx firenook init --adopt --dry-run` checks your project without changing anything. If something behaves differently from the official emulator, please tell me here or open an issue. That's the most useful feedback I can get.

projects.title: Show HN: Securing GrokBot
projects.author: maximelb
projects.summary: A friend at another tech startup was telling me how they started using Grok Bot and loved it. Surprise surprise they also got pretty worried about what it's doing and the visibility they had. Digging under the hood, hey there's a Linux VM and a Chrome browser. This is really cool because it essentially defines an environment that is really similar to a typical workstation. After some playing around I got the LimaCharlie EDR installed, the Chrome LC EDR installed and the email provider connected to the LC Email Security. Took a few iteration to make it all smooth but it works great on the free community edition! So you get to see what is executing on the box, where the bot is browsing and emails in and out. I built a couple detections using AI and just made it a doc in our documentation so you can just tell Grok Bot: """ Secure my Grok Bot with LimaCharlie by following https://docs.limacharlie.io/grok-bot/ """ The TL;DR; of what it does: - all of it goes to your own private tenant - installs a linux EDR on the box - installs a Chrome extension that is essentially an EDR in your browser - if you want, connects your gmail (any IMAP is supported really) and is like an EDR for the email - If you want it sends the alerts to your Grok Bot (I'm curious to see the advantage of a feedback loop here), or it's available on the web app.limacharlie.io The other option I left in was to leave the CLI authenticated on the Grok Bot. The interesting bit about that is that because the CLI has 100% coverage of the platform, you can ask the Grok Bot to start setting up new alerts, investigate alerts, configure everything... I tried to make it more generic for other AI agents where I have no idea what the environment is: https://docs.limacharlie.io/2-sensors-deployment/tutorials/s... though disclaimer I have not tried it yet, but it's not rocket science and more frontier AI models are now rocket scientists. The advantage that Grok Bot has is that it fundamentally allows things to execute on the VM and talk out. The other ones (Muse, Dots) seem to proxy every single thing and generally be extremely difficult to extend. Anyway, hope it helps some of you! (and yes, got it to make a cool video :D) https://youtu.be/yZZuBgKWd1k

projects.title: 开源了一个 agent 技能，能把扫描件和手机拍的文档重建成矢量 PDF（附对照实验）
projects.author: 3351666087abc
projects.summary: 做了一个给 Claude Code 和 Codex 用的技能，能把扫描件或手机斜拍的文档重新做成干净的 PDF：文字可以搜索、复制，图表和流程图是矢量图，放大不会糊，版式贴近原稿。它不是在图片上加一层 OCR 文字。 我还做了对照实验。测试页由程序生成，每页都有标准答案，类型有练习册、表格、图表、流程图、表单和双栏文章，其中一半是斜着拍、带阴影的手机照片。每页按标准答案给文字、版式、图形和矢量比例打分，1.0 为满分。同一个需求，每个模型做两次，一次不用技能，一次用。下面是两份 9 页文档上的结果，技能从没在这些页面上调过参： | 模型 | 不用 | 用 | |---|---|---| | Haiku 5.5 | 0.841 | **0.997** | | Fable 5.1 | 0.837 | **0.997** | | Sonnet 5.5 | 0.994 | **0.998** | | Opus 5.5 | 0.993 | **0.998** | 耗时：Sonnet 做 9 页从 25.7 分钟降到 16.2 分钟（快 37%），Haiku 基本持平（ 9.4 → 9.0 ），Opus 和 Fable 变慢（ 13.3 → 14.7 、10.0 → 14.7 ）。每个模型只有两份文档，耗时仅供参考。 最早的版本只是一份详细的说明，效果不明显。起作用的是把 agent 容易出错的步骤交给脚本： - 模型看到的是缩小后的图，位置和小数字只能估。现在由脚本按像素测量，没把握的词裁出来放大，每页汇总成一张校对图。 - 模型发现不了自己漏了什么。现在每次重建都会和原稿叠在一起比对，逐页报告还缺什么。 - 模型倾向于少做步骤。现在起草所有页只要一条命令，改一个错字只要在 JSON 里写一行。 失败的版本也写在 README 里了，比如有一版让 Sonnet 退步，原因是照片比例算错了。评测代码也开源了，欢迎用别的模型试试。 安装：在 Claude Code 里依次执行 `/plugin marketplace add 3351666087/scan-to-vector-skill` 和 `/plugin install scan-to-vector@scan-to-vector-skill`，也可以用 README 里的一行命令安装（支持 Claude Code 和 Codex ）。脚本需要 Python 3.10+ 和 tesseract 命令，依赖见 README 。MIT 协议。 GitHub： https://github.com/3351666087/scan-to-vector-skill 局限：测试集是合成的英文印刷页，手写和中文都没有测过。起草脚本调用 Tesseract 时不指定语言，只用英文模型，内置字体也只有西文，所以起草脚本目前处理不了中文页面，只装中文语言包不够。它按页消耗 agent 的时间，如果只需要能搜索的文字，直接用 OCRmyPDF 更省事。

projects.title: Show HN: Rivermark, a superfast AI graphic design canvas
projects.author: thegeomaster
projects.summary: Hi HN, Agents can nowadays design UI very competently, but the wider question of graphic design is largely unsolved. On one side, you have image models like ChatGPT images, which are high-quality but recognizable and barely editable. On the other hand, you can use LLMs and accept results that, well, look like UI. I've been working on Rivermark for a few months now to tackle this issue. It's an infinite canvas with an agent that excels at creating on-brand visual content for socials, marketing, and to some extent print. The agent is extremely context-aware and fast (we call it a "short horizon" agent). It will ingest anything and run with it - from Google Sheets copy/paste to .zip files with brandkits or photo sets. Everything is editable manually like in Figma too. We found it works best for people who are not designers but who know what looks good. MCP features to connect it to your agents are coming soon. We're powered by superfast inference at almost 1000 tokens per second and a custom realtime harness, meaning the agent is non-blocking and always responsive, and even has a non-turn-based voice mode that you can just talk into. We have some teams and early power users shipping work with it and are learning a lot. There have been numerous engineering and product challenges to even get here - I'd be happy to talk about them!

Kairos addresses two of the biggest problems facing traditional decisioning tools: a lack of labeled data to train on and dealing with fraudsters that are constantly changing their tactics. 1. Traditional fraud solutions use ML models such as XGBoost to detect fraud, but these models are dependent on quality labeled data which many businesses do not have. We address this by using “System One” decision models in additional to traditional models such as XGBoost and logistic regression. This allows you to incorporate plain language questions such as “Is this a throwaway email” into your decisioning, bypassing the need for large amounts of labeled data. This also allows you to capture aspects of fraud that are more unstructured, which is something that XGBoost models struggle with. 2. Fraud teams are facing off with live players that are constantly changing their behavior to bypass the detection logic they have in place. You can train a detection model or define a ruleset once, but it will become obsolete in a matter of weeks as fraudsters figure out what your detection logic is. This means that you need a team regularly training models and updating rules based on new fraud patterns. Typically this takes a large data science/ML team. Kairos addresses this by introducing an MCP server, so that your agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) can define a decision workflow, train models on your data, and pick the variant that performs best. You can self-host Kairos with Docker or use the hosted version at https://kairos.finic.ai

projects.title: Show HN: Spooler – a simple, managed message queue
projects.author: gobwas
projects.summary: Hi Folks, I'm Sergey, founder of Spooler ( https://spooler.sh ) -- a durable, fully managed message queue, inspired by the simplicity of Go channels. Why? Whenever I needed a queue for something, it often felt that adding one would be a bigger project than the solution. Existing systems offered far more than I needed, while using a relational database usually meant inventing queue semantics on the go. What I really wanted was just a send and recv with retries. After nearly six months of engineering, I'm really happy to share the result with you. How it works: you send a message to the queue, you recv it leased; when the message processing is done you acknowledge it, if the lease times out, the message gets back to the queue to be delivered again or into the failed state on too many retries. There is an atomic ack-and-send: you can acknowledge a message and append another in a single operation. You can model state machines with it: a queue is a state, a message in the queue is an object in that state, and ack-and-send is the transition. Each Spooler queue lives in a spool: a storage isolation unit (hence the product name) with its own write-ahead log and replication. That means that durable operations succeed only after the log entry is durable on disk and confirmed by the required number of replicas. Feel free to try it out! There is a docker image for testing it locally: https://docs.spooler.sh/local (it uses the same API but with in-memory storage, which means messages live only as long as the container runs). Spooler has an open-source CLI and Go library and there is also a repo of agent skills for it. The server itself is closed source, so there is no self-hosted options today. Please do share your thoughts about the product -- I really hope it feels ordinary to use. Sergey.

projects.title: Show HN: ArchDocs – Shared context and verification for engineers and AI agents
projects.author: AylonArmstrong
projects.summary: Hi HN, My name is Aylon and I'm building ArchDocs. I started building ArchDocs in late 2024 as an architecture diagramming tool with reusable references and objects (still exists today and is usable). As I've been using AI to code more and more, one of the things I've run into is that my agent doesn't have enough context around past decisions or findings that could affect an implementation, causing some nasty side-effects like redundant investigations, incorrect assumptions, repeating previously caught mistakes and ultimately wasting precious tokens. Let's say for example, you need to do a migration that affects 10 backend services. Your agent starts working on the first one and during the implementation and verification process, it discovers an issue that will undeniably affect the other 9 services. The next agent can start on the second service without knowing what was learned on the first. There's another problem I run up against time and time again. I need a dependable way to verify and log what an agent has done, the outcome of that and any deviations or issues that arise from it, so I can tell whether the change actually did what I intended. Enter Design Docs inside ArchDocs. The workflow is simple. You or your agent can craft a spec and ask questions for people to answer. Writing the implementation plan comes next, followed by doing the actual work. While you or your agent works, you track important milestones, deviations, decisions and more in the work log. Need to pause or have someone else do the work? No problem, craft a handoff or let ArchDocs AI do it for you. Finally, you or your agent logs a summarized version of what was done and how it was verified in an evidence of work submission. In that migration example, your agent can mark the issue in the work log as a "finding" and that will then be surfaced when future agents execute on the other 9 services. On the verification side, you may ask, "How does this help if the agent or engineer is just writing down their verification?" This is a good question and that's only one part of the verification. We have this concept of Agent attested (paired with human verified) and human attested. The last pillar and the most important is ArchDocs' own independent, automated verifications. Right now, we just have GitHub tracking for check results but we will soon be expanding this into so much more. Imagine one of the automated verifications is that a specific log with a specific attribute shows up in Datadog. Maybe even a specific event showing up in PostHog. There's a lot of ways we're going to take this and we're excited to share them once done. You can explore an example design doc without signing up. It includes the spec, implementation plan, work log and verification evidence: https://archdocs.io/templates/design-doc-example

projects.title: 【工具自荐】SimplerEmail：做了多个独立产品后，我给自己做了一个域名邮件工具
projects.author: yandong2023
projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个从自己维护多个独立产品的需求中做出来的小工具：SimplerEmail。 为什么会做这个工具 我们自己做了几个独立产品，每个产品都需要一个正式的联系地址，比如 support@产品域名。产品逐渐多起来后，邮箱也跟着变多了。 麻烦的地方在于：有些产品只是偶尔收到几封咨询，但依然要分别配置邮箱、查看来信，再确认应该用哪个产品的身份回复。对于一个人维护多个产品的场景，邮件量不一定大，管理入口却越来越多。 我们希望每个产品都保留自己的域名地址，同时让维护者继续使用每天已经在看的那个邮箱。于是做了 SimplerEmail，先解决一个具体的问题：多个产品的邮件，汇总到一个日常邮箱处理，回复时仍使用各自的产品地址。 它如何工作 举个例子，你同时维护两个产品： support@product-a.com hello@product-b.com 接入这两个域名并开启转发后，来信可以统一转发到你已验证的常用邮箱。完成产品地址的发信配置后，直接在常用邮箱中回复转发邮件，SimplerEmail 会通过回复中继，以对应产品的地址发给客户。也可以在网站中查看邮件、回复和主动写信。 这样，每个产品仍有独立的对外身份，自己日常只需要关注一个主邮箱。 产品截图 下面是官网首页及邮件工作区预览，图中的产品名称与邮件内容为演示数据。 目前支持的功能 多个自有域名接入：为不同产品使用各自的域名邮件地址。 来信转发到主邮箱：转发目标需要先验证，并在设置后开启转发。 以产品地址回复：支持在常用邮箱回复转发邮件，也可以在网站中处理邮件。 按产品整理邮件：提供产品筛选、待回复状态和可编辑分类标签。 API 与 MCP 发信：应用或兼容的 MCP 客户端可通过已验证的产品地址发送通知；API/MCP 密钥仅用于发信，不提供收件箱读取权限。 免费额度与接入要求 免费版支持 10 个自有域名，每月共享 100 次邮件操作，包含 API 与 MCP。收信、自动转发、回复分别计数，例如收到一封邮件、转发一次、回复一次，共使用 3 次操作。邮件量增长后可选择付费套餐。 域名需要自行持有，首次接入需要验证所有权并按指引配置 DNS。修改 MX 会影响该域名的邮件路由，已有邮箱的域名需要先检查现有配置。 产品聚焦个人维护多个产品的邮件场景，目前不提供 IMAP、POP3 或日历。常用邮箱回复中继要求发出的邮件带 DKIM 签名，具体适配条件见官网说明。

projects.title: Show HN: An experiment in automated long-horizon builds with AMQP 0.9.1
projects.author: mxplusb
projects.summary: My cofounders and I are in the process of spinning up an AI integration lab, and over the last year we've consumed billions of tokens across multiple American, European, and Chinese models as a force multiplier for building out our products. However, despite our extensive technical expertise, we've still discovered there are long-term ramifications to heavy agentic AI usage. So I decided to run an experiment for us: given a specification, can an LLM fully, concretely, and correctly implement an internally consistent, linearizable distributed system to the same quality as a human? This repository is the outcome and showcase of that experiment, complete with the entire session history, including tool outputs. To make this project, I only gave the LLM the AMQP 0.9.1 specification and a few requirements: it must use clustered Raft, and it must support up to 9 nodes (light ceiling, but not the final limit). I picked an older but less well-known protocol as it provided a simplistic base with a wide range of features built on top; a messaging platform more than just a broker. While the specification itself is fairly old, it is still very viable and valuable today for a wide range of uses. For our uses, I chose Switchboard as the experiment as our products are sealed appliances and we need a stable, scalable message broker that's embeddable into our existing apps (embedded distributed systems are easier when it's all the same binary), deployable as a standalone service, and understandable enough by everyone that debugging and diagnosing it is easy. This experiment is not designed to compete with RabbitMQ or other solutions (altho it is a love letter to my former vmware/Pivotal coworkers who worked on RabbitMQ), and I will be maintaining it for our own use cases. I wrote it in Rust specifically because our code base is written in Rust. While I may talk about the hands-on design, build, and testing of the project as "automated" and "with long horizon capabilities", it is not vibe-coded slop. There are hundreds of cross-platform and cross-architecture tests, and full Jepsen linearization tests on Linux - I am going to put this software into high-compliance production environments and I need it to be stable. In finality, I hope you find my little experiment in automated, spec-driven, long-horizon builds interesting and insightful. Contributions are welcome, if desired, but with the age of the protocol I don't expect any real consumers other than our lab. Happy message passing!

projects.title: Show HN: Hanging Context – news by an agent, for other agents
projects.author: bshivarthy
projects.summary: Back in 2022 I was building a data and news site for family offices, private wealth and investment managers. We used the early OpenAI models to write data-driven stories covering the markets for art, collectibles, luxury goods and other cultural assets. Mid-2024, a well-known AI company asked to license our stories. The big labs were signing licensing deals with media companies. This is when it clicked. The biggest reader of news wasn’t going to be people. It was going to be their agents, and agents have unlimited hours of attention. So I built Synorb. It reads thousands of sources and turns fresh content objects into Manifests (structured claims with provenance) that are dispatched via Streams anchored to organizations, people and datasets. Hanging Context is an experiment on top of that. Could an agent read our streams and stand up a news site for other agents to read and find trustworthy? The first version with a home-brewed Hermes agent was cumbersome so I tried Instinct and Muse when they released and settled on Muse as I found it better at narratives, images. An agent runs the site. I wrote this post. How it works: Every 12 hours Muse reads hundreds of new Manifests published in our streams, then writes a new edition for the site. Every article produced cites the Manifests it used. Before it publishes an article, an API checks it for quotes. They must appear word for word in a cited Manifest. Every paragraph needs to be backed by a citation and sources have to be under 24 hours old. Muse doesn’t probabilistically determine what to trust - if 3 or more different sources back it, it’s "Confirmed". Otherwise it’s "Reported". At the time of writing, the site had 30 of 45 articles Confirmed. Here’s an article with 3 sources cited; the panel at the bottom shows what was checked: https://hangingcontext.com/stories/2026-11-02/agent-stack-re... It costs almost nothing to run as I'm using Muse on the free plan, and since it only needs to pull Manifests, reason and write, it can run just fine. To try it, just add https://hangingcontext.com/mcp to Claude, Cursor or any MCP client. No sign-up or key required. Setup: https://github.com/Synorb/hanging-context . What I’m trying to figure out: When I saw the early pull numbers by agents, I thought this could be a lead-gen micro-site for Synorb. I’ve built those before for human focused consumer and enterprise products. Conversion is now the challenge. For a casual daily read, Hanging Context already does all the work. I don’t want to be annoying and cut coverage or show previews. So my plan is to just keep it free and try grow the number of agents pulling daily. Full Disclosure: Synorb is my paid product, and Muse reads through its own Synorb account. Curious if your agents would trust news written by another agent and what I can do to improve the odds.

projects.title: Show HN: Remene – Understand your MRI and prepare questions for your doctor
projects.author: molcode
projects.summary: We’re building Remene around a familiar problem: you receive your MRI images and a radiologist’s report, but making sense of them is difficult in many cases. Now, of course, many of us use ChatGPT, Claude, or other services like these to understand those terms and double-check the findings, just to feel a little more sure about what we’re reading. One thing we discovered during our early tests is that this is not that easy to do with ChatGPT, Claude, or others. If you’ve already tried it with your own MRI, you’ve probably run into some of the same issues. A study can have hundreds of images, and some we tested had over 2.000. Getting all of those into a regular chat session is a problem. Even if you convert the DICOM files yourself, you can still run into upload and subscription limits. You keep trying, uploading smaller batches, asking it to fix something, and meanwhile you’re using up your subscription allowance before you’ve even got to the questions you wanted to ask. You may have some luck with ChatGPT building a simple DICOM processor for the task. But these are scripts written for a one-off job, and getting something that runs is not quite the same as getting something you can trust with different MRI studies. From what we’ve seen, even though DICOM is a well-established standard, studies can come with all sorts of differences that these scripts don’t handle well. Sometimes you end up debugging the converter when all you wanted was to understand your scan. But let’s say its superintelligence manages to build a perfect DICOM converter. There’s still the privacy question. DICOM files store lots of personal information: your name, date of birth, ID numbers, the clinic name, and more. It’s easy to think you’re just uploading files without realizing what else is inside them. What we’re doing differently is putting a lot of effort into the DICOM processing pipeline. We de-identify the files (removing or replacing personal details), and keep the images and the metadata like which series they belong to, the view, whether fat suppression was used, etc. That way, we can reduce the personal information sent to the AI to the maximum. We keep sex information and age as a range, for example 30–39 rather than an exact age, because these can provide useful context for the analysis. Secondly, we’re making sure the AI pipeline can get to the images it needs to analyze. We feed it images from the main MRI series, dozens and even hundreds, and give the agents tools to request additional images or information, or look at the same structure from another view. And lastly, we also want this product to be a tool for understanding, but also for checking for potential misses or errors. We’re human, and sometimes it’s easy to miss a detail, especially when there are so many images in an MRI and so little time to go through them all. This doesn’t replace the radiologist or your doctor, and the AI can make mistakes too. It’s meant to be an additional check on your scan and report, with anything it flags being something you can discuss with your doctor. The most critical point here is that this product is educational. It doesn’t give medical advice. It explains what the AI thinks it sees, what it can’t assess, and what might be worth discussing. In the end, you’ve probably already spent some time staring at those images, reading the report again, and wondering what to ask. We hope Remene makes that part much easier, so you can go into the appointment with your questions ready.

projects.title: Show HN: Globalize.now – translations that land in your pull request
projects.author: artursvonda
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Arturs, cofounder of globalize.now. Our view is that the best developer tools don't ask teams to change how they work. They show up where the work already happens. Dependabot doesn't make you log into a dependency dashboard; it opens a PR. Localization mostly works the other way. A TMS brings its own dashboard, upload and download loops, review queues, and a sync step someone has to own. Liam and I spent years at Lokalise watching teams reshape their process around that. It fits a localization department. It doesn't fit a small team shipping daily. So we built translation into the PR itself. Connect your GitHub repo, open a PR as usual, and we translate the new or changed strings, run QA checks, and commit the locale files to that same PR. The feature and its translations get reviewed and merged together, so nothing ships half-translated. If you'd rather keep translations separate, pick a branch instead: every push to it gets its own translation PR. Either way, files stay in your repo in your library's own format, so there's nothing to sync and nothing to migrate off. This can look trivial. A GitHub Action that sends changed strings to an LLM is an afternoon's work, and plenty of you have built one. The afternoon version is where it starts, though. Keeping terminology consistent, not re-translating what hasn't changed, catching broken placeholders and plural forms, and not paying for the whole catalog on every push is the part that keeps needing attention. We'd rather own that so you don't have to. Glossaries, style guides and translation memory are built in, and they push the output toward what a good localization team would produce. We run it on our own site, which is mostly long-form content (blog posts). Adding Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese (about 5,600 strings each) took 8 minutes and cost €31. If your app isn't i18n-ready yet, an agent skill sets up the library, extracts hardcoded strings and connects the repo: npx skills add globalize-now/globalize-skills Pricing starts at €5/month plus usage ~€0.15/1000 chars depending on size of glossary, style guide etc. No seats. We think this "tool in the middle" pattern applies well beyond translation (e.g. accessibility fixes, docs drift, language consistency). We'd like to hear where you think it breaks down, and how it works for you in practice. Try it at https://globalize.now .

projects.title: 【开源自荐】vmr：Rust 重写后，一个命令管理 80+ 种 SDK，还能装 conda-forge 的 3 万多个包
projects.author: moqsien

github.name: gvcgo/version-manager
github.description: 🔥 A general version manager for thousands of SDKs.

projects.summary: 最新版本：v0.8.1（2026-11-08） 收录说明：2024 年第 299 期收录过本项目的 Go 版本（当时支持 40 多种语言）。2026 年 11 月发布 Rust 重写版 v0.8，命令和磁盘布局保持兼容，但安装后端换成 pixi 的 Rust 组件（rattler），并新增了下面这些能力，故再次自荐。 一句话：一个命令行工具，同时管理 80+ 种语言和工具的版本，还能直接安装 conda-forge 上的 3 万多个包。 为什么需要它 nvm、pyenv、sdkman、rustup 各管一摊；想装 ffmpeg、cmake、ripgrep 之类的工具又要另找包管理器；conda 则是另一套几百 MB 的体系。vmr 把这些收进一个二进制：不需要管理员权限，所有版本放在 ~/.vmr 下，切换版本只是换一个软链接。 亮点 80+ 种语言和工具：Go、Node.js、Python、JDK、Rust、Zig、Bun、Deno、dotnet、PHP、R、Lua……以及 ripgrep、fzf、lazygit、neovim、ffmpeg、cmake 等常用 CLI 工具，共 82 个插件。 背靠 conda-forge：内置 pixi 同源的 rattler 后端，直接读取 conda-forge 的 repodata（linux-64 子目录压缩后约 60 MB），本地 zstd 缓存后用求解器装完整依赖闭包，不需要预装 conda/miniconda。按 2026-11 抓取的 repodata 统计，linux-64 + noarch 去重后共 34,598 个包名、约 120 万条构建记录；VMRPIXICHANNEL 可换清华等镜像。 项目级版本锁定：在项目里执行 vmr use -l node@20.11.0，会写入 .vmr.lock；之后 cd 进目录自动切到锁定版本，离开自动还原。lock 文件提交进仓库，队友进入目录即对齐版本。 切换立即生效，也能隔离：shell 集成让 vmr use 后的版本在当前终端马上可用，不用新开窗口；vmr use -s 只对当前子 shell 生效，退出自动恢复；vmr freeze 导出清单，新机器 vmr use -f 批量装回。 Rust 重写，下载更稳：单一可执行文件，多线程分块下载 + SHA256 校验，支持反向代理、本地代理与 HTTP(S)PROXY。Linux、macOS、Windows 的 x8664 与 aarch64 都有预编译包，Homebrew、Scoop、APT、pacman 可直接装。 vmr mcp：以 MCP 服务把「查版本、装版本、取 PATH / GOROOT」交给 AI 客户端调用。 快速上手 bash macOS / Linux brew install gvcgo/tap/vmr Windows: scoop bucket add gvcgo && scoop install gvcgo/vmr eval "$(vmr init zsh)" # 启用 cd 钩子，切换立即生效 vmr plugins # 支持的 SDK vmr search go && vmr use go@1.22.0 vmr use -l node@20.11.0 # 项目内锁定版本 vmr use -s python@3.12 # 只对当前会话生效 vmr search -p lua # 查 conda-forge vmr use -p lua@5.4.6 # 安装任意 conda-forge 包，无需装 conda

projects.summary: 开源协议：Apache-2.0 ACCP（Agent Collaboration Control Plane）是面向研发团队的自托管 AI 协作管理平台：人在 Web 控制台管任务、项目资料、成果验收和高风险工具审批；Agent 通过本地 Bridge（MCP 工具）、REST 或 Go SDK 接入，领取任务、读取固定上下文快照、汇报进度并提交可核对的成果（含 Git 引用）。每项任务仍由人类负责人接受或退回。它不替代 Cursor / Claude Desktop / Codex 等客户端，也不内置大模型，只做任务 / 上下文 / 验收这一层。 为什么需要它 团队里产品用 GPT、前端用 Cursor、测试用别的客户端时，个人变快了，整体却常卡在对齐：需求散在聊天里、字段名对不上、「完成」标准不一致。ACCP 把协作收成一条可追溯流程：任务有负责人与依赖，资料按版本发布并绑定执行快照，成果经核验后再验收。 主要能力 任务与依赖：指定负责人、执行代理、验收条件；按依赖衔接（例如接口约定发布后再解锁前端接入） 版本化项目资料：需求 / 接口 / 规范按版本发布，Agent 按本次快照读取 Agent 接入：MCP Bridge、REST、Go SDK / CLI；常用工具包括领取任务、读快照与资料、汇报进度、登记成果、查事件等 成果与审批：查看正文与 Git 引用、核验来源；网关内高风险工具操作可走独立人工审批与审计 私有部署：Docker Compose 单机部署；PostgreSQL + NATS JetStream；企业 OIDC 登录 技术栈 Go + React / TypeScript + PostgreSQL + NATS JetStream + OIDC；前端 Vite / HeroUI / Tailwind。本机可用 docker compose 快速起试用环境（仓库 README 有步骤）。 当前状态（诚实说明） 已具备任务、资料、执行、成果、审批与审计的协作闭环，以及团队管理与运维工具，适合受控试用。Claude Desktop 与 Codex 有单人双客户端样例验收记录。正式版本分发、目标规模容量验证和完整恢复验收尚未完成；成果正文当前以文本与 Git 引用为主（正文上限 256 KiB）。欢迎试用与反馈，也欢迎共建。

projects.title: [开源分享] MemDock：Claude Code 和 Codex 的双助手工作台，支持会话互转、记忆和 Skills 管理
projects.author: LingyiChen-AI

github.name: LingyiChen-AI/MemDock
github.description: Desktop app to manage Claude Code and Codex memories, skills, sessions and usage

projects.summary: 用 Claude Code 和 Codex 久了，我常遇到两件事。测试命令早就换了，新会话还在按旧规则跑。想更新一个 Skill，又要先翻目录，确认当初装在了哪个工具里。我做了 MemDock，把这些散在不同地方的记忆和 Skill 放到一个桌面工作台里。 规则散在哪，先找得着 在「记忆总览」里，可以按全局或项目搜索 CLAUDE.md、AGENTS.md 和 Claude Code 的自动记忆，也能浏览只读的 Codex 记忆库。规则文件支持分栏编辑和版本回滚。想知道一条规则从哪来，可以在项目记忆图谱中查看关联并跳回来源。 每周翻一遍，有依据再更新 比如项目已经换了测试命令，你在对话里纠正过助手，规则文件却还写着旧命令。可以设成每周提取一次，让 MemDock 从近期对话里找出值得补充的经验和需要修订的规则。也可以每天定时提取，或者手动运行。 提取结果先进入「待审核记忆」。你可以对照旧内容、新建议和原对话，再决定采纳、改完再采纳，或者驳回。采纳后才写回文件。 我到底装了哪些 Skill？ 「Skill 管理」会列出 Claude Code 和 Codex 已装的 Skill，区分全局和项目范围，也能看来源和文件。Superpowers 这类插件会按包展示。可以从 GitHub、本地目录或 ZIP 安装，在两个工具之间复制，也可以检查更新、批量更新或从备份恢复。 换台电脑，规则和清单一起带走 旧电脑可以把记忆和 Skill 安装清单同步到自己的 GitHub 私有仓库。新电脑登录同一个账号，从同一个仓库拉取记忆，再按清单补装缺少的 Skill。有冲突时可以逐块处理，外观和记忆提取等偏好也能单独恢复。 平时写代码，还能用到这些 对话和终端。按项目查看两边的历史会话，支持 Claude Code 与 Codex 双向转换。可以切换图形聊天和原生命令行，也可以开独立的分屏终端。 代码和并行开发。在对话旁搜索、编辑文件和查看 Git 差异。多条任务可以各开一个 Git Worktree，分别开发，做完再合并。 用量和额度。查看两个工具的 Token、估算费用和活跃热力图，支持导出 CSV，也可以选择开启实时额度查询。 飞书连接。用自建机器人在飞书里调用本机助手，按项目和使用者控制访问权限。 桌面设置。检测或安装助手 CLI，设置语言、主题和开机自启，安装版支持自动检查更新。 MemDock 支持 macOS 和 Windows。可以先打开一个常用项目，看看有哪些规则还在用、哪些 Skill 已经装了。

projects.author: dooly6276

github.name: dooly6276/claude-bulkhead
github.description: Run many Claude Code sessions on one machine safely: no killed dev servers, port clashes, RAM or disk freezes, or mixed-up commits. Zero-dependency hooks.

projects.summary: GitHub · dooly6276/claude-bulkhead 开源协议：MIT 同时开多个 Claude Code 会话，或者让子智能体并行干活时，它们共用同一台机器，容易互相干扰：一个会话用 pkill node 按名字杀进程，别的会话的开发服务器和测试一起被杀掉；两个会话抢同一个端口；几个会话同时跑测试把内存耗尽；有的会话在别人正在改的目录里执行 git add -A 或 git checkout，把对方改到一半的内容提交进去。claude-bulkhead 是一个 Claude Code 插件，由一组 PreToolUse 钩子组成，在命令执行前拦截这些操作，并把拦截原因和替代命令（例如改用 PID 终止、换一个空闲端口、改用 git worktree）直接返回给智能体，不需要等人确认。它还会排队执行重型命令，使用所有会话共享的内存预算，并清理已结束会话遗留的服务进程。它解析的是命令字符串，不是沙箱。只依赖 Node，没有其他依赖。 0.2 版新增 bulkhead scan：把 ~/.claude/projects 里过去的会话记录中的 shell 命令重放一遍，看这些守卫本来会拦下什么。只读，不向任何地方发送数据，令牌会被遮蔽。作者在自己的机器上扫描了两周的记录（7.0 GB，约 10.1 万条 shell 命令），耗时 39 秒：最多同时开着 13 个会话，有 507 条命令本来会被拦下，其中 25 条是在另一个会话正在修改的目录里执行的 git add -A。 安装： /plugin marketplace add dooly6276/claude-bulkhead /plugin install bulkhead@bulkhead

projects.title: 【开源自荐】AITerminal：带可扩展插件中心的 AI 运维终端
projects.author: Amo-Zeng

github.name: Amo-Zeng/AITerminal
github.description: AI 运维终端：本地 PTY / SSH、多标签 AI 接管、交互式 CLI 与插件中心。Apache-2.0。

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个我维护的开源项目 AITerminal：带可扩展插件中心的 AI 运维终端，采用 Apache-2.0 协议。 它把本地终端、SSH 和 AI 操作放在同一个桌面界面里。重点是让开发者把自己的运维经验、排障流程和常用工具封装成插件，按需安装、组合和分享。 插件中心目前支持： 扩展 AI 和终端能力：插件可以提供参数化工具、AI 指引、模型适配器、任务事件和界面面板，也能接入标准 MCP 服务（stdio / Streamable HTTP）。例如用 Docker 工作台查看容器状态、执行巡检和读取交互日志，用通知插件订阅任务结果。 开发与分发：提供插件 SDK、类型定义，以及创建模板、校验、打包命令；支持导入本地开发目录或插件包、配置自定义 HTTPS 插件源和恢复历史版本。 按标签启用：不同终端标签的插件实例、配置、AI 上下文和任务相互隔离，可以为不同服务器配置不同的工具组合。 可参考的内置插件：目前有 10 个，包括系统巡检、Docker 工作台、Git 时光机、任务通知，以及无需模型 Key 的终端宠物和运维闯关。既有运维用途，也提供面板、事件和会话状态的开发示例。 应用支持 Windows、Linux 和 macOS；Windows 本地终端默认使用 WSL Ubuntu，当前 macOS 安装包为 Apple Silicon。使用 AI 时配置自己的模型 API，支持 Chat Completions、Responses 和 Messages 格式；也支持 Codex、tmux 等交互式命令。 欢迎试用、反馈问题，也欢迎开发者一起完善插件系统，贡献运维工具、MCP 集成、模型适配器或有趣的小插件。

github.name: Firefly-0423/Firefly-Agent
github.description: ✨ Firefly lives on your Windows desktop: chat with her, or let her and 12 partners read files, write code and run commands, with your OK on every step.

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一个我开源的桌面端 AI 项目：Firefly-Agent 为什么做这个项目？ 市面上现有的桌面宠物大多只能简单闲聊，聊几句就容易“失忆”；而真正能读写文件、改代码、跑终端的 Agent 工具，往往又只是一个冷冰冰的命令行或聊天框。 我想尝试打破这层割裂：把「有温度的 Live2D 角色陪伴」和「有严格安全边界的本地多智能体工作台」真正融合进同一个桌面窗口里。 核心工程设计与亮点 1. Chat / Work / Code 三态同窗与克制陪伴 右下角常驻 Live2D 模型，但拒绝做“烦人的弹窗机器”：调用底层工具干活时，她会自动切换成认真的「工作表情」；内置主动关心话题，但如果检测到你在忙未回复，绝不会连续打扰。 切入 Work 与 Code 模式后，可直接接入本地文件系统、Git、LSP 以及 Obsidian 知识库。 2. 主从式多 Agent 并行委派（1+12 ）协同 面对复杂的多步骤任务（如同时统计代码函数、检索多篇本地笔记并交叉比对），主代理（流萤）不再单线程死磕，而是按需从内置的 12 个角色子代理中委派帮手开启子会话并行处理，最后由主代理对照原文做统一核对与汇总。每个子代理均可独立绑定不同的大模型服务。 3. 本地三层加密记忆链与 d3-force 记忆星图 为了解决桌宠“聊完就忘”和“胡乱幻觉”的问题，所有上下文与事实全部加密落盘在本机 SQLite 中，拆分为 S（近期语境）/ M（核心事实）/ H（历史检索） 三层记忆配合 RAG 检索。 在设置页中，系统会将她记住的关于你的事实，实时渲染成一张以“你”为中心的 d3-force 动态记忆关系星图。 4. “动手之前先问你”：自研 Harness 循环与安全沙箱 底层基于 TypeScript 与 Rust 原生辅助模块（app.rs）构建，原生支持 MCP 协议（stdio / SSE / Streamable HTTP）与插件扩展。 所有的文件写入、命令执行、内置浏览器操作均受控于权限拦截器（支持命令审批卡片、目录隔离与 TUN 模式下的 fake-ip 拦截）。执行完毕后，繁琐的调用日志会自动折叠为一行干净的时间线摘要。 5. 零门槛的在线交互预览 为了让不想立刻下载安装包的朋友也能直观感受交互逻辑，我复用同一套前端代码构建了免安装的在线体验网页，点开即玩。 相关

github.description: A macOS-first local information broker for AI agents, with selected-field access, Chrome intake, and origin-bound credential handoff.

projects.summary: 在线演示与产品介绍（含 33 秒演示视频与交互式沙盒）： 在使用 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 或 OpenClaw 等本地 AI Agent 处理网页表单、登录和二次验证（2FA）时，用户往往不得不把密码写进明文 .env、在对话框里反复粘贴个人地址，或者把账号和信用卡上传到云端 Bot Vault。 Agent Autofill（Apache-2.0 开源）是一个运行在 macOS 本机的个人数据金库与 MCP（Model Context Protocol）信息代理服务，核心设计是“只给 Agent 当前任务所需的最小字段，其余留在你的 Mac 上”： 1. 本机钥匙串加密存储：个人资料（区分 Home / Work 语义）、网站登录凭据和支付卡信息保存在本机 AES-GCM 加密的 SQLite 数据库中，主密钥与邮箱授权令牌存储在 macOS Keychain。 2. 免明文 CSV 的 Chrome 本地导入：支持扫描本机 Chrome 多配置目录（Default、Profile 1 等）的地址簿与密码管理器，通过本机回环界面（127.0.0.1）确认语义并筛选后再写入正式库，无需导出明文 CSV。 3. 密码不进大模型上下文（credential.use）：提供配套 Chrome 扩展的单次、绑定目标域名（Origin-bound）令牌交接机制，由扩展在校验当前页面域名后填入密码，原始密码不会进入 LLM Prompt 或日志。 4. 限定范围的 2FA 验证码读取：支持从只读 Gmail API（gmail.readonly）、IMAP 邮箱以及 macOS 本机信息（Messages chat.db，含 Sonoma/Sequoia attributedBody 二进制流解码）中提取最近一次验证码，并在读取后标记已消费以防重放。 5. 严格的只读信息边界：仅提供信息读取与提案，绝不代为跳转网页、点击提交按钮、发送消息或自动结账。 可以先运行完全使用虚构数据、无需配置账号或网络的交互演示： bash uv tool install git+ agent-autofill demo 一行命令接入本地 MCP 客户端： bash agent-autofill mcp-install --client claude # 支持 claude / cursor / codex / antigravity

projects.title: [开源] agent-hub：统一管理 Codex / Claude Code，还能通过微信派活
projects.author: hengtu2012
projects.summary: codex-hub 最近升级为 **agent-hub**，现在可以用一致的方式管理和操作 Codex 、Claude Code 。 项目地址： https://github.com/someonegg/agent_hub 平时同时开几个 coding agent ，除了切终端，还需要找会话、看进展、补充要求、处理确认。agent-hub 把这些操作集中到一个本地 Web 工作台里，也提供 CLI 和技能，让另一个 AI 来完成调度。 可以把它用成一个轻量级的个人 **Super Agent 工作台**： - **Router （主控）**：理解需求、拆解任务、分派工作、跟进结果。 - **Worker**：由 Codex 、Claude Code 等会话负责具体执行。 - **agent-hub**：提供统一的会话管理、交互和结果读取入口。 主控可以通过 `ahub-control` 技能创建或恢复会话、发送任务、读取回复、查看终端，以及处理中断和交互确认。具体怎么拆任务、结果是否达标，由主控判断。 最近试了一个挺有意思的入口：**用腾讯 WorkBuddy 做主控，从个人微信操作 coding agent 。** 这样出门后也能在微信里了解电脑上的工作进展，进一步通过同一套接口派活、补充要求、收集结果。 接入也比较直接： 1. 电脑上运行 agent-hub ，配置好 Codex / Claude Code 。 2. 安装 WorkBuddy ，在助理设置里扫码绑定个人微信，无需企业微信或 App ID / Secret 。 3. 执行下面的命令，找到技能目录，让 WorkBuddy 安装 `ahub-control`： ```bash ahub-cli skill path ahub-control ``` 4. 在微信中明确说“使用 ahub-control”，再描述要操作的项目和任务。 远程使用需要电脑保持开机、联网，WorkBuddy 和 agent-hub 持续运行。 我的想法很简单：把自己常用的 AI 连接起来，组成一支个人工作团队。既能自己在工作台里操作，也能让主控 agent 帮忙调度。 欢迎同样在用 Codex / Claude Code 的朋友试试，也想听听大家平时是怎么管理多个 agent 、怎么做主控与 Worker 分工的。

projects.title: Show HN: stardelt.io – a self-hosted lakehouse on k8s (pre-alpha)
projects.author: schwarztrinker
projects.summary: I am pretty honest: there are a ton of vibecoded projects around, and I made another one... great huh? I'm working as a data platform engineer in Germany. My day job is basically spinning up & running lakehouse platforms on US hyperscalers for SMB and some DAX companies. I mean, data engineers like to work on these platforms but since some time I really have ethical concerns about it - like: - vendor lock-in - high costs (because of cloud costs - and in most cases you are not able to connect your own metal if you have one) - non-EU vendors... - other open-source solutions have high license costs for LDAP etc. pp. That's why is started to build my own opinionated data lakehouse platform in my spare time (tbh I also started learning agentic engineering and what harnesses are..), only curated from open source projects already available. The building blocks are pretty straightforward imo: - Iceberg tables on whatever S3 storage you already have - Trino for SQL and Spark Connect for jobs - Airflow for schedules, plus notebooks, Kafka streams and dashboards - One web UI and one API over all of it - stuff around like OIDC, secrets management etc. It's fully pre-alpha. But I want to use it as an internal pitch project at my current employer to push agentic engineering & the idea of creating our own data platform for our non-hyperscaler customers. Site: https://stardelt.io Code: https://github.com/stardelt I'm happy to hear what you think about it :) Cheers, Martin

projects.title: Herdr 的终端界面能把事情做好。Shepi 让你在 Mac 上用得更愉快。
projects.author: wisteen
projects.summary: 同时让几个 AI 编程 agent 做事，难点不只在于怎么给任务。一个在本机改接口，一个在检查测试，服务器上还有一个处理数据。你得不断切回终端，确认谁还在工作，谁正等着你。 我做的 [Shepi]( https://shepi.app/?v=20261107)，是 Herdr 的原生 Mac 客户端，与 Herdr TUI 实时共享同一套工作空间、标签页和 agents ，并支持简体中文、英文和日文。它不是另建一份桌面会话，也不需要你迁移现有工作。Herdr 负责维持 AI 编程 agent 的终端会话，Shepi 提供桌面入口，让任务、进度、产物和需要你参与的时刻，都有清楚的位置。 ## 01 · 现有的终端会话，打开就在那里 Shepi 和 Herdr TUI 连接同一个 Herdr server ，实时共享同一套工作空间、标签页和 agents 。在终端启动的会话，会直接出现在 Shepi ；从 Shepi 启动的，也能在终端里看到。两端可以同时使用，不用迁移，不是复制一份，也不会为桌面界面另开一套独立会话。 Claude Code 、Codex 、OpenCode 、Gemini CLI 、Cursor 、Copilot CLI ，仍然运行在完整的真实终端里。旋转标记表示工作中，空心圆表示空闲，状态也有文字；当前输入的窗格是更浅的卡片。想用桌面窗口就打开，想回 TUI 就回去，接着做的是同一份工作。 ![Shepi 窗口：左侧是工作区和 agent 的边栏，顶部是标签页，中间是三个窗格，底部是状态栏。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/window.webp) *工作区、agent 状态和真实终端，在同一个窗口里。（指南原图）* ## 02 · 需要你时，不必靠反复巡视发现 当 agent 停下来请求确认，例如准备部署、删除或安装时，侧栏、窗格标题和状态栏会亮起琥珀色； agent 提供操作信息时，也能看见它要执行什么。收起侧栏仍有横幅，切到其他应用会收到 macOS 通知，知道谁停了、工作了多久，点击查看就能回去。声音沿用 Herdr 的提醒时机，远程机器也一样。我希望你能专心做别的事，而不是守着输出等待。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/needs.mp4) ## 03 · 把背景和选项讲清楚，再请你决定 在你要求时，agent 可以发来带背景、选项及各自后果的提问卡。你从任何窗格都能点选，或写自己的回答，答案直接回给对应 agent 。它也能打开网页、在名称下报告进度，或在自身上下左右打开测试和日志窗格，标明归属而不抢键盘焦点；远程 agent 同样可用。这些动作让确认与检查留在工作旁边，不必从长段输出里寻找入口。 ![claude 问 “Deploy to staging?”，卡片位于窗口右上角，写明了情况，有三个回答，每个都说明会做什么，Deploy 标为“建议”，还有一个可以自己写回答的输入框； claude 窗格泛着琥珀色光。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/ask.webp) *先了解情况，再选择下一步；也可以直接写自己的回答。（指南原图）* ## 04 · 一项工作结束，把下一项交接清楚 有些任务适合分段完成。前一个 agent 做完后，可以留下交接提示，结束当前窗格，再由一个新的 agent 在同一位置接手。也可以安排稍后开始，或等另一个 agent 完成后再执行。安排在机器上运行，关闭 Shepi 也会继续；需要你介入时，仍然停下来等待。我想提供的是清楚的接续位置，而不是假设开发过程不再需要人判断。 ## 05 · 回来时，知道它进行到哪一步 一句“还在工作”，不足以解释任务的进展。Agent 可以把计划放在 Shepi 里，当前步骤显示在名称下面，状态旁有累计工作时长。把指针停在步骤上或点击，就能展开全部步骤、进度条、当前项与每一步的耗时。关掉窗口再打开，这些进度仍然保留。回来时可以先读清位置，再决定是否需要翻完整输出。 ![边栏：带分支和 agent 徽标的工作区，以及显示标志、已工作时长和当前步骤的 agent ；其中一个 agent 的任务卡片在旁边打开，进行到第 3 步（共 4 步）。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/agents.webp) *当前步骤留在侧栏，完整计划和耗时可以展开查看。（指南原图）* ## 06 · 不只听“完成了”，也看看实际改动 检查结果时，我希望能顺手对照代码，而不只是读 agent 的总结。Shepi 可以查看本机和远程项目自上次提交以来的未提交变更。通过状态栏，或 prefix 后按 d 打开 diff ，按习惯选择并排或单列阅读；看完按 Esc ，就回到原来的窗格。这里做的是查看，不负责暂存或编辑代码，把后续操作留给你自己的工作流程。 ![差异视图：左侧是更改的文件，右侧是更改内容。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/diff.webp) *把 agent 的说明与实际变更对照着看。（指南原图）* ## 07 · 远程机器，加入同一个工作视野 如果任务跑在服务器上，可以直接在 Shepi 内添加 SSH 机器，使用已有的密钥。输入主机后，由 Herdr 连接；机器会以自己的标题加入侧栏，下面是它的工作区和 agents 。每个工作区都有需介入、工作中、完成和空闲的数量。本机改页面、远程处理数据时，不必把机器边界变成另一套窗口管理负担。 ![窗口上方的“添加机器”表单。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/machines.webp) *从应用内添加 SSH 机器，和本机任务一起查看。（指南原图）* ## 08 · 在 agent 旁边，留一个能动手的 shell Agent 改完接口，你可能想自己跑一次测试；排查异常时，也可能需要持续看日志。Shepi 可以向旁边或下方拆分真实 shell ，让这些操作紧邻当前任务：跑测试、追踪日志，或用命令打开 PR 。新窗格在原布局中展开，不必另找一个终端窗口，也不用把自己的检查命令塞进 agent 的输入流。协作不只有观看，随时动手也应当方便。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/split.mp4) ## 09 · 输入之前，清楚自己正对着谁 几个 agent 并排时，发错位置比少看一条输出更让人分心。Shepi 用更浅的卡片标出当前输入窗格，只有这里有闪烁光标，标题也写着 agent 的名字。其他窗格保持完整亮度，不会因为失去焦点就暗下去，仍然方便对照输出。可以点击切换，也能用 prefix 加 h 、j 、k 、l 移到相邻窗格，让注意力和键盘去向保持一致。 ## 10 · 布局变零碎，一次把空间分匀 工作过程中不断拆分、拖动，窗格难免变得有大有小。有时你并不需要精确设计比例，只想让每个任务重新获得差不多的阅读空间。prefix 加 = 会让当前标签页里的窗格均分空间，无论此前怎样拆分或调整，都能把布局收拾齐整。我希望整理窗口是一个随手动作，不必在真正的任务之外，再花时间经营一套布局。 ## 11 · 把当前问题看大，也保留原来的位置 读一段长日志，或专心看一个 agent 的结果时，可以用 prefix 加 z 把当前窗格放大到整个窗口，文字保持原位。其他窗格只是留在后面，并没有被关闭；角标、标签页和窗格标题会提醒你正在缩放。再按同一个键，或点击还原，就能回到原布局。临时专注不需要先拆散工作现场，看完也不用重新排列其他任务。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/zoom.mp4) ## 12 · 重复输入，交给知道等待的宏 切换模型、重启开发服务器，或顺序输入几条命令，可以收进一个宏。它不只是连续敲字符，也能等前一步的内容出现在屏幕上再继续：例如等待模型菜单出现，再移动和确认。可以让当前 agent 编写、试运行并告诉你按键，也能让它修改、列出或删除；愿意自己写，就在 Settings 里完成。本机和远程都能用，把明确重复的动作收起来，留出判断的精力。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/macro.mp4) ## 13 · 它做出的页面，就放在旁边检查 让 agent 展示页面，网页就能在旁边打开，本机开发服务和远程服务器提供的页面都可以。你能直接点击交互，也有后退、前进、刷新和在外部浏览器打开的入口。即便光标落在网页输入框里，Shepi 的 prefix 仍然有效，按 Esc 可以把键盘操作交还窗口。检查页面和继续终端工作，不必来回寻找各自藏在哪个应用里。 ![一个 agent 在旁边的窗格中打开了它的开发服务器页面。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/web.webp) *开发服务器与页面并排，方便检查刚完成的结果。（指南原图）* ## 14 · 相关内容放近，终端继续运行 日志应该靠近正在排查问题的 agent ，测试也可以移到更方便对照的位置。拖住窗格标题，松手前就能预览布局：交换两个窗格，或放到另一个的上、下、左、右。拖到其他标签页可以跨 tab 移动，悬停后还能精确选择落点；放到加号上，就单独建立一个标签页。位置改变时，终端始终继续运行，整理现场不必打断工作。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/move.mp4) ## 15 · 记住一点线索，就能找回任务 不一定每次都记得任务在哪台机器、哪个工作区里。Shepi 的统一搜索覆盖机器、工作区、agents 、窗格和最近输出，本机与 SSH 机器都在同一个入口。输入一两个词，可以组合查询，也不必遵守固定词序，找到结果后按 Return 就能进入。无论记住的是任务名字，还是刚看过的一段输出，都可以从线索回到工作位置。 ![打开的查找，输入了查询，结果按类型分组。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/find.webp) *同一个搜索入口，同时找任务位置和输出中的线索。（指南原图）* ## 16 · 刚才的位置，不用再找一遍 有时并不需要完整搜索，只是切出去看了一眼，想回到刚才的窗格。Cmd E 会列出跨机器最近使用的位置，按最近顺序排列，并默认选中刚离开的那一个。再按 Return ，就回去了。列表也支持输入文字查找，和搜索一样使用。处理几个交错的任务时，这样的小入口能让临时切换更直接，不必每次都重新辨认侧栏和标签页。 [查看演示视频]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/recent.mp4) ## 17 · 错过的事情，留在收件箱里 Shepi 开着而你离开时，不是每条通知都会当场看到。期间 agent 完成任务、需要介入或发来问题的事件，会留在查找旁边的收件箱里，Dock 也显示数量。点击其中一条，可以直达对应窗格；查看那个窗格之后，提醒才会清掉。我希望回来之后有迹可循，先接住等待处理的事情，而不是重新巡视所有终端，猜测离开时发生了什么。 ![托盘按钮下方的收件箱，列出在你没在看时需要你处理或已完成的 agent 。]( https://shepi.app/guide/img/zh/inbox.webp) *错过的事件留在这里，回来接着处理。（指南原图）* ## 18 · 关掉窗口，工作仍有自己的位置 退出 Shepi 、关掉窗口，或关闭 Herdr TUI ，都不会停止底层 server 中的 agents 。远程服务器上的任务，在这台 Mac 睡眠时也继续运行。重新打开 Shepi ，可以回到原来的工作位置；如果中间断开连接，状态栏还会告诉你有多少窗格发生了变化。窗口是入口，不是任务存在的前提，可以离开，也能在回来时接着做。 Shepi 继承 Herdr 的 prefix 和键位，默认是 Control-B ，也支持鼠标。我希望保留终端的直接，同时把多任务、远程连接与需要人参与的环节讲清楚。如果你经常同时使用几个 AI 编程 agent ，或在 Mac 与服务器之间切换，这就是我想照顾的工作场景。 整个应用支持简体中文、英文和日文，可以跟随 Mac 的语言，也可以在设置里切换，立即生效，不用重启。菜单、设置、提问卡、提示消息和通知等界面内容都有对应翻译；终端里的 agent 、命令和输出则保留原样。网站和用户指南也提供这三种语言，阅读说明与实际操作可以用同一种界面语言。 Shepi 适用于 macOS 15 及以上，支持 Apple silicon 和 Intel Mac ，需要 Herdr 0.9.3 及以上。它是我独立开发的产品，非 Herdr 官方应用。

projects.summary: 我是作者，自荐一个自己做的开源项目：Onion Board，Windows 上的音效板（soundboard）。 打游戏或语音聊天时按一个键，语音频道里的人就能听到你放的音效。这类工具通常要装虚拟声卡，再把聊天软件的麦克风换成虚拟设备。Onion Board 默认换了个做法：给你现有的麦克风加一个 Windows 音频效果，把音效直接送进去，语音软件和游戏继续用原来的麦克风，不用改选设备。 因为改的是 Windows 里的麦克风，用这个麦克风的软件一般都能听到。我主要在 Discord、Zoom 和游戏里测过，KOOK、YY 这些国内常用的语音软件还没测过，欢迎反馈。 全局热键：在游戏里也能触发，还支持游戏内浮层和 MIDI 设备。 变声器：内置多种声音，说话时实时变声。 文字转语音：打字后由电脑语音念出来，可以用 Windows 自带的语音，也可以接本机的 TTS。 简体中文界面：已经翻译好，不用另装语言包。 有几点先说清楚： 只支持 Windows 10 / 11。 第一次开启“直接送进麦克风”时，Windows 会要一次管理员权限。不想这样的话，也可以改用虚拟声卡。 安装包还没有代码签名，Windows 可能会弹出警告。 程序会发送一个匿名的每日使用计数，可以在设置里关掉。 这个项目是我借助 AI（Claude Code）开发的，提交记录里也看得到。 免费，没有广告，不用注册账号，采用 GPL-3.0-or-later 许可证。

projects.title: Show HN: Rui, orchestrating 100 agents in 2.5 MB of RAM
projects.author: divyanshgolyan
projects.summary: Hi HN, I've built Rui (cotton in hindi), an agent runtime built for memory efficiency. The main design choice is that sessions share a host rather than each being a process. Agents are state in DB and the host handles the active work through a share event loop. LLMs are getting better at coordination and teams (swarms) of agents are coming. Memory is getting expensive and my machine is always using swap. We cannot be wasting hundreds of MBs of RAM for an orchestrator (AKA the harness) of LLMs and tools. More information on the architecture and measurement methodology is at https://divyanshgolyan.com/posts/hundred-agents/ I'd love feedback about this design boxing me into a corner and any large tradeoffs I'm not seeing!

projects.summary: A few days back I posted here asking about how people were using AI / doing agentic coding (see: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50366117 ). The one challenge I found, however, was that the comments were almost impossible to parse: some users answered my questions in the format I provided, others answered in any order, but either way it was really hard to get a picture of who was using what from that thread alone.
